jobs.description:
Duties Description Kirby Forensic Psychiatric Center (KFPC), an Office of Mental Health (OMH) forensic facility is recruiting a Deputy Director, Psychiatric Center 2 – Operations (DDPC 2 – Ops) to serve as the Director of Inpatient Services.
  

  

Duties
  

The Director of Inpatient Services serves as an essential member of KFPC’s Executive Leadership Team. Under the general direction of the Executive Director, the Director of Inpatient Services is responsible for the non\-medical clinical management of KFPC’s inpatient forensic hospital. The Director of Inpatient Services will design, develop, evaluate, and ensure the effective operations of all KFPC’s adult treatment programs including:
  

  

* Establishing and maintaining safe environments for patient care with a focus on evidence\-based programs, cultural competence, and community care.
* Participating in the development of KFPC’s short and long term goals.
* Establishing policies and procedures to ensure efficient and effective service delivery.
* Monitoring and overseeing staffing, assignments, and work schedules to ensure quality patient care.
* Ensuring service delivery complies with OMH guidelines, values, and regulatory agency standards.
* Maintaining working relationships with external organizations to maximize resources and implement program goals.
* Supervising and coordinating activities of subordinate managers.

  

  

  

  

Minimum Qualifications Education
  

Master's degree in a mental hygiene discipline (including physician assistant, occupational therapy, physical therapy, social work, speech pathology and audiology, communication disorders, psychology, recreation therapy, rehabilitation counseling, education, nursing), hospital administration, community mental health, business or public administration or other administrative area specifically related to health care, behavioral or social science or a valid license to practice medicine in New York State or Canada.
  

  

AND
  

  

Experience
  

Seven (7\) years of administrative, consultative, or supervisory experience in a mental health program, three (3\) years of which must have been managerial experience, including one or more of the following:
  

  

1\. One (1\) year of experience in a position comparable to Clinical Chief of Service or Director of Mental Health Rehabilitation;
  

  

OR
  

  

2\. Two (2\) years of experience in a position as administrative head of a multidisciplinary treatment team;
  

  

OR
  

  

3\. Two (2\) years of professional, supervisory, or administrative experience in the development, operation, and/or implementation of the mental health service delivery system for State facilities, counties, or local/private agencies in three (3\) or more of the following areas: program development, management procedures, community organization, resource planning, funding, program proposals, advisory boards, consumer and community advocacy and intergovernmental relations.
  

  

Additionally, all candidates must be eligible to participate in Federal health care programs (e.g., Medicaid). Individuals excluded from participation in these programs will not be considered.  

  



Additional Comments About KFPC
  

KFPC, located on Ward’s Island in New York City, provides inpatient treatment and rehabilitation to pretrial defendants who were deemed unfit to stand trial and were court ordered for restoration of fitness to stand trial and individuals who have been found not guilty by reason of insanity. KFPC is committed to supporting underserved individuals and delivering treatment with respect for each individual's privacy and rights along with activities and initiatives to reduce disparities in access, quality, and treatment for underserved populations.
  

  

About OMH
  

OMH operates the largest state mental health system in the country, with 23 hospitals, 90 clinics, two world\-class research institutes, a secure residential center, and a network of community services. OMH hospitals are all Joint Commission\-accredited and recognized as among the best mental health hospital systems in the United States. OMH believes everyone should have an equal opportunity to achieve mental wellness. This means implementing services and policies to reduce disparities in access, quality, and treatment outcomes for historically marginalized, underserved, and unserved populations.
  

If you would like to join KFPC and contribute to a workforce dedicated to public service, we offer:
  

* Generous paid time off, including thirteen (13\) vacation days, eight (8\) sick days, and five (5\) personal days accrued during the first year of employment; thirteen (13\) paid holidays each year.
* Option to choose a NYS health insurance plan that meets your needs.
* Dental and vision coverage.
* Enrollment in the New York State and Local Retirement System (NYSLRS) or a voluntary defined contribution plan.

  

Notes:
  

Plus $4,150 Location Pay.

**Storehouse West, Inc. \- Rio Rancho, New Mexico**

**Part\-Time \| 25 Hours per Week \| $40,800 Annual Salary**

Storehouse West is seeking a compassionate, energetic, and community\-minded leader to serve as our next Executive Director.

Storehouse West is a community\-focused nonprofit organization serving residents of Sandoval County who are in need. We provide nourishing food, children's clothing, assistance with utility bills, and referrals to other community resources.

Our Executive Director is the day\-to\-day leader of the organization and works closely with our Board of Directors, employees, volunteers, donors, and community partners to carry out the Storehouse West mission.

The Executive Director is the chief administrative, supervisory, and development officer of Storehouse West and reports directly to the Board of Directors.

This is a 25\-hour\-per\-week position, with the Executive Director expected to be present during all Storehouse West office and food\-distribution hours. The position also requires attendance at monthly Board meetings and participation in community activities, including Chamber of Commerce events and meetings with current and prospective donors. Some of these responsibilities may occasionally take place outside regular Storehouse West office hours.

This is very much a hands\-on leadership position. We are looking for someone who enjoys working with people and is just as comfortable talking with a donor or community leader as working alongside our employees and volunteers to solve an everyday operational problem.

· Lead and support our paid staff and volunteers, including recruiting, training, supervision, performance management, and recognition.

· Work with the Board to develop organizational priorities, plans, policies, and budgets.

· Develop and carry out an annual fundraising plan in partnership with the Fund Development Committee.

· Seek grants, donations, sponsorships, and other financial and in\-kind support.

· Develop and maintain relationships with major donors while building a sustainable base of individual donors.

· Oversee fundraising events, donor records, proposals, and required reports.

· Work with the Finance Committee and Board to maintain sound financial practices and operate within the Board\-approved budget.

· Maintain organizational records and help ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements.

· Oversee Storehouse West facilities and equipment and maintain a safe, clean environment.

· Represent Storehouse West throughout the community and help increase awareness of our mission.

· Support our website, social media, newsletters, annual report, and other community communications.

· Attend Board meetings, provide regular Executive Director reports, and work cooperatively with the Board and its committees.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who genuinely cares about serving people and understands that the success of a community nonprofit depends on relationships \- with clients, employees, volunteers, donors, community partners, and the Board.

**Strong candidates will have:**

· Experience in nonprofit leadership, management, community service, or a related field.

· Experience supervising employees and working with volunteers.

· Fundraising, donor\-development, or grant\-writing experience.

· Strong organizational, communication, leadership, and problem\-solving skills.

· The ability to build and maintain productive community partnerships.

· An understanding of budgeting and basic nonprofit financial management.

· Computer proficiency, including word processing, email, internet/social media, and familiarity with financial\-management software such as QuickBooks.

A bachelor's degree in business, public relations, nonprofit management, or a related field is preferred. Significant relevant leadership and management experience may be considered in place of a degree.

Experience with food\-assistance programs, food banks, nonprofit compliance, fundraising, grant development, or service on or with a nonprofit Board is also highly desirable.

**Salary:** $40,800 annually ($3,400 per month)

**Schedule:** Approximately 25 hours per week

**Location:** Rio Rancho, New Mexico

**Benefits:** This position does not currently include employee benefits.

The Executive Director is expected to be present during Storehouse West office/distribution hours and attend monthly Board meetings. The position also includes occasional community, Chamber of Commerce, donor, and fundraising activities outside normal office hours.

How to Apply

· A current resume

· A cover letter explaining their interest in Storehouse West and the Executive Director position

· Professional references

**Applications should be submitted to: executivedirector@storehousewest.org**

The position will remain open until filled. Applications will be reviewed as they are received.

***Storehouse West, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer.***

Pay: From $40,800\.00 per year

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Executive Director. Reports to: Board of Directors as a whole. Supervisory responsibility: all employees, directly or through designated supervisors; oversight of contractors and professional advisers within approved agreements. The President is the ordinary Board liaison, not a substitute for collective Board authority.

FLSA classification: Exempt only while the actual duties, salary basis, and applicable salary requirements meet a lawful executive or administrative exemption. CHWW shall document and communicate the classification under Handbook Section 1\.C. In the absence of a documented valid exemption, the position is nonexempt and all compensable time must be recorded and paid.

Position Summary

The Executive Director is CHWW's chief employed administrator and is accountable for the overall management, financial stability, safe and reliable water service, personnel, regulatory coordination, member service, and execution of Board policy. In a small rural utility, the role includes both management and hands\-on administrative work, filling reasonable operational gaps, and developing dependable backup systems. The Executive Director is expected to anticipate needs, bring material issues to the Board early, and obtain appropriate professional assistance rather than perform unlicensed work or assume unrestricted authority.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

1\. Leadership, planning, and daily administration. Translate the mission and Board decisions into work priorities, procedures, budgets, and measurable objectives. Coordinate treatment, distribution, billing, customer service, finance, HR, technology, and administrative functions. Resolve cross\-department issues; assign work; monitor completion; and maintain continuity when staffing is limited. Recommend organizational improvements and sustainable service standards.

2\. Board and corporate governance. Prepare agendas, management reports, budgets, proposed policies, and decision materials with the President and Secretary\-Treasurer. Present accurate operational, financial, compliance, personnel, and risk information without obscuring adverse developments. Support meeting notices, elections, membership records, minutes, corporate filings, and required member communications while preserving the Secretary\-Treasurer's accountability. Implement approved actions and maintain an action\-item record. Obtain counsel's advice on governing documents, records requests, open\-government applicability, major transactions, and disputed authority. Maintain a current governing\-document and amendment register, distinguish charter requirements from ordinary bylaw quorum rules, and obtain legal review of election terms and adoption thresholds. Maintain complete approval records for each election, amendment, and corporate action.

3\. Financial stewardship. Develop annual operating and capital budgets and multiyear financial and asset\-replacement plans. Monitor revenue, cash flow, costs, reserves, debt service, covenant compliance, and budget variances. Coordinate bookkeeping, payroll, tax filings, financial statements, and the independent annual audit with qualified staff and advisers. Recommend rates, fees, deposits, and financial policies to the Board with supporting cost and affordability information; implement only lawfully adopted changes. Ensure invoices and payroll are accurate and timely, and maintain independent approval and reconciliation controls even when personally covering financial tasks.

4\. Funding, grants, and lender relations. Identify suitable financing, grants, technical assistance, and reimbursement opportunities. Coordinate applications, feasibility information, matching resources, environmental and procurement conditions, reporting, draw requests, and closeout. Track restricted funds and avoid commitments before required approval. Maintain productive relationships with lenders, grant administrators, and financial advisers. Do not promise funding or eligibility before verification or incur debt outside Board authority.

5\. Drinking\-water and environmental compliance. Maintain a complete register of the utility's facilities, permits, operating conditions, sampling and reporting duties, inspection findings, and renewal dates. Ensure adequate licensed treatment and distribution staffing and backup coverage appropriate to each system classification. Coordinate compliance with the Safe Drinking Water Act, applicable Florida DEP and other public\-health requirements, Northwest Florida Water Management District requirements, and other applicable authorities. Require qualified review of sampling, operational logs, consumer confidence reports, public notices, water\-use reports, cross\-connection control, and corrective actions. Track applicable lead and copper, PFAS, and other rule changes with qualified advisers, identifying each adopted requirement and its effective date. Oversee continuing service\-line inventory verification, updates, customer notices, replacement planning, and related funding documentation. Maintain current compliance and funding records.

6\. Operations and infrastructure. Oversee source\-water availability, treatment, storage, distribution pressure, water quality, metering, asset condition, preventive maintenance, inventory, fleet readiness, and water\-loss control through qualified staff. Review work orders, outages, repairs, inspections, alarm response, and maintenance backlogs. Plan timely replacement or expansion of wells, tanks, mains, pumps, controls, and other assets. Ensure current maps and asset records, physical security, appropriate easements and access, and reliable supply and repair arrangements. Do not promise fire\-flow capacity, system extensions, or new connections without technical and legal verification. Require field verification of mains recorded as inactive or abandoned, reconcile system maps and material inventories, and maintain valve, hydrant, backup\-power, and surge\-protect

**Executive Director Opportunity**

**Kokomo Rescue Mission \| Kokomo, Indiana**

Lead a trusted organization. Transform lives. Shape the future.

The Kokomo Rescue Mission is seeking an experienced and passionate Executive Director to lead a well established, Christ\-centered nonprofit into its next season of growth and impact.

Located in Kokomo, Indiana, a growing industrial city and farming community in north central Indiana, the Mission is approximately one hour north of Indianapolis.

Founded in 1953, the Kokomo Rescue Mission has more than 70 years of history serving individuals and families that are homeless and hurting. Today, the organization operates with an annual budget exceeding $3\.5 million, with approximately $1\.8 million coming through direct community donations. This is a testament to the strong relationships and confidence the Mission has built throughout the community.

The Mission operates three homeless shelters, serving men, women, and women with children. In 2025, the Mission provided an average of 326 meals each day and served an average of 122 overnight guests each night.

The organization is also entering an exciting new chapter of community engagement. Its new Engagement Center expands the Mission’s reach beyond traditional shelter services by providing practical assistance, connecting individuals with community partners and resources, and offering showers and laundry facilities to the broader community.

The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to lead a respected organization with a strong foundation, committed staff, generous community support, and significant potential for continued growth.

This leader will help shape the Mission’s future while strengthening its ministry, expanding community partnerships, stewarding its resources, developing its team, and ensuring that the organization remains focused on its calling to serve the homeless and hurting.

For the right leader, this is more than an executive position. It is an opportunity to step into a 70\+ year legacy, lead a growing nonprofit, build upon strong community relationships, and help shape the future of social services in Kokomo and beyond.

If you are a strategic, relational, mission\-driven leader who is ready to make a lasting difference, we invite you to consider joining the Kokomo Rescue Mission by submitting your resume to ksalsbery@rescuekokomo.org or visit our website at https://kokomorescuemission.org/

**Position Summary:**

The Executive Director of the Kokomo Rescue Mission provides strategic leadership, ensuring the organization's vision, programs, and financial sustainability align with its mission. He or She oversees staff, fundraising efforts, and community relations while advocating for the Mission’s work and securing resources. Additionally, the Executive Director ensures compliance with regulations, manages crisis situations, and leads long\-term strategic planning for the organization's growth and impact.

**Core Competencies:**

* Teamwork
* Operations Management
* Personnel Management
* Spiritual Leadership
* Financial Management
* Development
* Administrative Oversight

**Primary Duties and Responsibilities (includes but not limited to):**

**Administrative Duties:**

* Responsible for the spiritual environment and growth of all Mission programs by approving the development of new programs as necessary to meet the needs of the community.
* Evaluate current programs to see if they still are reaching the needs of the community.
* Prepare for and attend Board of Director's meetings and executive committee meetings.
* Carry out Mission policy; create the same in emergency situations where needed.
* Recommend to the Board new or significant changes to ministries.
* Attend skill and spiritual enrichment conferences and seminars that will benefit the Mission.

**Operational Management:**

* Have a comprehensive knowledge of the principles and practices of program, personnel, and budget administration necessary to the efficient operation of the entire organization.
* Hire and terminate employees. Responsible for hiring the right people into leadership.
* Responsible for the operation of administrative and departmental functions according to the Organizational Chart.
* Meet with the Lead Team on a regular basis to maintain effective communication within the ministry.
* Maintain continuous interface with leadership to insure proper and effective staffing in order to carry out the Mission’s purposes.
* Administer evaluations for the staff that directly report to the Executive Director and maintain a salary review program.
* Assess need and implement necessary staff education.
* Preside over weekly staff meetings.

**Public Relations Duties:**

* Represent KRM through speaking engagements, conferences, church groups, service clubs, other community organizations, television, radio, and newspaper interviews.
* Network with community leaders, businessmen, industrial executives, etc.
* Cooperate with governmental and other private help organizations in assisting those in need.

**Financial Duties:**

* Be ultimately responsible for Mission finances.
* Oversee the fundraising initiatives and campaigns of the organization.
* Direct preparation of Annual Budget for Board approval.
* Work with Staff in preparing the final operating budgets for approval by the Board of Directors and regularly monitor financial reports to see that the departments stay within the budget parameters.
* Review monthly financial reports and be prepared to answer any questions that arise at Board meetings.
* See that the Mission acknowledges all donations to the ministry with a receipt and thank you.

**Education or Skill Set:**

* Bachelor’s degree preferred in nonprofit management, business administration, public administration, organizational leadership, social work, human services, ministry/theology, or a related field and/or minimum of 5 years of executive leadership experience in a related field.

Barry County Christian Schools and BCCS Foundation

Barry County Christian Schools is seeking a committed Christian leader to serve as its next Executive Director.

For 55 years, BCCS has partnered with families to provide Christ\-centered education in Barry County. Today, BCCS operates two K–12 campuses in Hastings and Middleville. Our mission is “Inspiring and Equipping our students to achieve their God\-given potential.”

The Executive Director is the senior administrative leader of the organization and reports directly to the BCCS Executive Board. This individual provides leadership for both school campuses, directly supervises both campus principals, and hires personnel throughout the organization.

The Executive Director also provides leadership for the BCCS Foundation and oversees its business operations.

This is more than an administrative position. We are seeking someone who believes deeply in Christian education, leads with humility and courage, builds strong relationships, develops other leaders, and is prepared to guide BCCS into its next season.

We build on a unique foundation: Our reach is global; we discover through best\-in\-class science; we protect through work on the ground with local and indigenous people; we inspire through our world\-class zoos, aquarium, and education programs; and we leverage our resources through partnerships and powerful policy influence. Our more than 4,000 diverse, passionately committed team members in New York City and around the world work collectively to achieve our conservation mission.
  

  

**JOB DESCRIPTION**
  

  

**Position**: Executive Director, Global Finance Operations and Controls
  

  

**Reports to**: Vice President \& Comptroller, Vice President of Global Finance
  

  

**Position Managed:** Regional Controllers
  

  

**Location:** United States (Flexible)
  

  

**Program/Sector**: GCP/Global Finance\\S
  

  

**Scope**: Global
  

  

**Position Type**: Full\-Time
  

  

**Job Summary:**
  

  

The WCS Global Finance team is responsible for ensuring that key financial management accountabilities are in place across WCS’s 11 regions, in over 50 country programs and Global Conservations Program Headquarters (HQ) thematic based programs with a combined operating budget of nearly USD $250 million.
  

  

Executive Director, Global Finance Operations and Controls ensures the integrity of Global Conservation Program financial accounts and financial management processes, oversee compliance with WCS policies/procedures, and lead the audit and financial compliance function across the global regions of WCS. This position also has responsibility for assessing and building capacity of the regional and country finance teams by providing appropriate financial management training where necessary.
  

  

**Major Responsibilities:**  

  



* Provide operational leadership for global finance policies by translating approved standards into country and regional implementation across core accounting, cash management, grants, and cost allocation processes.
* Directly manage Regional Controllers, providing technical leadership, performance oversight, and ensuring consistent financial management quality across regions. Maintain a functional reporting relationship with country finance leads, ensuring alignment on financial management standards, technical guidance, and execution support.
* Serve as the primary field finance authority for donor compliance, reviewing budgets, grant submissions, cost allocations, and compliance risks, with escalation of institutional issues to the VP Comptroller.
* Coordinate and monitor execution of WCS internal audit activity in the field, including audit readiness, documentation, management responses, avpnd corrective action tracking.
* Develop and maintain country and regional financial risk profiles, identifying control weaknesses, compliance risks, and operational gaps to inform management prioritization.
* Design and deliver finance capacity\-building programs, including training, onboarding of senior finance staff, regional workshops, and ongoing professional development initiatives.
* Oversee the quality and timeliness of financial reporting from country offices, including review of reconciliations, reports, and donor submissions prior to escalation.
* Support ERP and systems implementation by gathering field requirements, coordinating testing, and driving change management across global finance operations.
* Maintain escalation oversight for high\-risk or institutional issues, including fraud risk, material control weaknesses, regulatory matters, donor audit proceedings, and policy exceptions requiring VP\-level review.
* Conduct periodic visits to WCS regional and country programs to support financial oversight, strengthen internal controls, build finance capacity, and foster strong partnerships with field leadership.
Qualification Requirements


* Advanced degree (MBA, MPA, or equivalent) in accounting, finance, or a related field required. Bachelor’s degree with CPA certification may be considered as an equivalent qualification given the seniority of this role.
* 10 years of progressively senior international finance and accounting experience in a complex global nonprofit organization, including demonstrated expertise in multi\-country operations, donor compliance, and field finance management.
* Solid computer skills with respect to Word, Excel, email and developing technologies in financial management.
* Experience with ERP systems.
* Experience with grants management.
* Models WCS’s Core Values: Integrity, Respect, Accountability \& Transparency, Diversity, Equity, \& Inclusion, Collaboration, and Innovation.
* Leads effectively in a global matrixed environment.

*Preferred:*
* CPA Strongly Preferred.
* Professional qualification such as Master of Business Administration (MBA).
* Proficient in Spanish or French language.
* Grants management experience with at least one of the following institutions: United States Government, United Nations, European Union, World Bank*.*

**Licenses \& Certifications:**
* Certifications such as Associate Chartered Accountant (ACA), Associate Chartered Management Accountant (ACMA) or Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) strongly preferred.

**The Opportunity**

The Executive Director leads Big Brothers Big Sisters of Fond du Lac County to ensure the agency's mission, strategy, values, and goals are achieved — and that our mentoring programs serve the youth of Fond du Lac County effectively and sustainably. This is a hands\-on leadership role spanning strategy, fundraising, board partnership, staff development, and community representation.

**What You'll Do**

* **Lead strategic planning** — Develop and drive the organization's strategic plan, working collaboratively with the Board and staff, and use performance data to guide decisions.
* **Grow philanthropic support** — Lead fundraising, donor engagement, grant development, and community partnerships. Build and sustain relationships with individual, foundation, and corporate donors.
* **Build a strong team** — Attract, retain, and develop talented, diverse staff. Create an engaged, high\-performing culture with clear goals and regular feedback.
* **Ensure financial health** — Oversee agency finances, fiscal controls, and long\-term sustainability, balancing financial strength with program quality.
* **Drive program impact** — Grow and support a strong base of volunteer mentors reflecting our community, with child safety as a top priority.
* **Partner with the Board** — Support Board development and governance, prepare regular reporting and the annual budget, and attend all Board meetings.

**What We're Looking For**

**Education \& Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Public Administration, Nonprofit Management, Human Services, Social Work, or a related field required.
* 7\+ years of proven results building an organization and achieving outcomes; nonprofit or youth development experience strongly preferred.

**Skills \& Abilities**

* Strategic thinking and systems\-level planning
* Entrepreneurial approach to limited resources
* Ability to manage for short\-, mid\-, and long\-term results
* Strong interpersonal, team\-building, and stakeholder management skills
* Excellent verbal and written communication
* Board development and fund development experience
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365; donor database/CRM experience (e.g., Salesforce) a plus
* Demonstrated integrity and sound ethical judgment, with proven ability to work effectively and build trust with diverse groups of people
* Strong service orientation across youth, families, volunteers, and community partners
* Experience leading organizational change and continuous improvement

* Ability to travel throughout the community and surrounding areas; occasional regional or overnight travel for conferences, training, and BBBSA meetings
* Valid driver's license
* Ability to sit/stand for extended periods, occasionally lift up to 25 lbs, and communicate effectively in person, by phone, and in writing

You'll lead an organization with a proven, measurable impact on kids in our community — with the support of an engaged Board and a passionate staff team behind you.

Benefits:

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

jobs.title: Global Executive Director
jobs.description:
Innovative Human Rights NGO Seeks Global Executive Director

About Asylum Access

We are human rights advocates who support forcibly displaced individuals and communities as they reclaim their rights, agency and power.

Our unique combination of legal empowerment, policy advocacy and global systems change creates conditions in which refugees can live safely, move freely, work on fair terms and go to school in supportive environments.

Our work transforms the traditional approach of endless humanitarian handouts to a sustainable solution that honors refugees’ freedom, dignity and autonomy, and empowers them to make choices about their own lives.

Asylum Access’ global team and family of local civil society organizations advocate to make human rights a reality for refugees around the world. Our national organizations are led and staffed primarily by community members in those countries, and there is strong mutual trust and respect between us and our clients. On the international stage, we work with established institutions to shift the global system to better uphold and promote refugees’ human rights. We can help catalyze and lead systemic transformation because, uniquely among NGOs in the refugee response sector, we focus exclusively on rights and governance.

Position Description

The global Executive Director is responsible for ensuring the Asylum Access family of organizations fulfills and advances Asylum Access’ mission around the world. This includes leading the organization’s global systems change portfolio; positioning the global organization to support strategic and effective national\-level legal empowerment and policy advocacy by Asylum Access national organizations; and guiding the organization in creating and pursuing a bold, cohesive vision toward a world where all displaced people enjoy all of their human rights.

Asylum Access values a collaborative approach to leadership. The global Executive Director is expected to work in close partnership with the national Executive Directors, who lead strategy and implementation of the mission at Asylum Access national organizations, to shape global organizational strategy, priorities, and performance. All four Executive Directors are responsible for stewarding Asylum Access’ vision and role within the global refugee response ecosystem; setting and executing organizational strategy within their particular remits and collaboratively across the global family of organizations; overseeing budgets and resource allocation; and ensuring strong programs, operations, and teams.

The successful candidate for global Executive Director will be visionary in outlook, with a broad understanding of displacement dynamics and political trends around the world – particularly in and affecting Africa, Asia and Latin America, where most refugees remain. They will be deeply collaborative in approach. They understand the importance of shared enthusiasm as a driving force, and the necessity of a cohesive leadership team to achieve meaningful impact in challenging circumstances. They are committed to understanding and supporting the contexts in which Asylum Access organizations currently work, and to identifying and advancing efforts in other contexts if/as this has the potential to magnify Asylum Access’ impact in creating the world we envision.

The global Executive Director is hired by, reports to, and serves at the pleasure of the Board of Directors, in accordance with the organization’s bylaws, and may serve as a nonvoting, *ex officio* member of the Board.

Essential Job Responsibilities

Key components of the global Executive Director role include, without limitation:

*Strategic Visioning and Leadership*

* With a consistent eye on the future, continually gather information and assess trends relevant to Asylum Access’ mission, and guide the organization to adapt accordingly – bearing in mind Asylum Access’ historic role at the forefront of paradigm shifts and operational innovations that support displaced people to reclaim their rights, agency and power.
* Together with staff and board leadership, and in consultation as appropriate with other stakeholders inside and outside the organization, craft and carry out a strategic vision in line with Asylum Access’ mission and values. This includes the development of theories of change and the development and implementation of multi\-year strategic, operational, and annual plans.
* Ensure the entire family of Asylum Access organizations maintains coherence and consistency with the organization’s mission, vision, values, and brand.
* Envision and develop governance structures that align with Asylum Access’ deep commitment to shifting power dynamics in service of a shared leadership model. This includes building consensus among the Executive Director team for decisions with organization\-wide impact.
* Inspire, motivate, and catalyze the development of staff at all levels of the organization.

*Global Oversight*

* Steward the cohesion of the global leadership team and the culture of collaborative leadership across the organization.
* Provide support and administrative supervision to National Executive Directors, and manage the hiring, onboarding, and termination of these positions in accordance with Asylum Access’ human resources protocols.
* Together with the National Executive Directors, lead oversight of Asylum Access’ impact to ensure all programs and advocacy are aligned with human rights principles and designed to effectively achieve Asylum Access’ mission, vision, and goals.

*Reputation and Influence*

* Steward and advance Asylum Access’ global reputation as a well\-known refugee human rights organization and as an important and effective actor in displacement response, human rights, and migration fields. In particular, give voice to on\-the\-ground impact within national organizations – and partner organizations where requested and appropriate – in international dialogue.
* Grow Asylum Access’ influenc

jobs.title: Director of Communications & Brand
jobs.description:
**Job Summary:**

The Director of Communications \& Brand is responsible for the strategic leadership of GEDP's communications, brand, and content function, shaping the organization's narrative, stewarding its visual and editorial identity, and ensuring that GEDP's work and impact are clearly and compellingly communicated to every audience it serves. The Director is the senior editorial, creative, and communications voice of the organization.

The Director leads a team of two manager\-level individual contributors — a Lead Designer and a Content \& Social Media Manager — and provides active creative direction, editorial oversight, and day\-to\-day management to both. The Director is not a production role; it is a leadership role that sets the creative and strategic direction the team executes against. This includes direct art direction of the Lead Designer's work, editorial direction of all content across GEDP's channels, and strategic oversight of GEDP's full digital and communications presence. GEDP anticipates adding a Content \& Social Media Coordinator as the function grows.

The Director of Communications \& Brand will lead GEDP through a significant period of organizational growth and public visibility, including an organizational rebrand, a capital campaign, and a destination marketing effort in partnership with the City of Easton. The Director serves as GEDP's primary liaison to outside communications, marketing, brand, and creative agency relationships.

**Job Duties \& Responsibilities:**

**Brand Strategy \& Organizational Narrative**

* Leads GEDP through an organizational rebrand in collaboration with the Executive Director, board, and outside creative partners; ensures the new identity reflects the organization's mission, voice, and strategic ambitions across all programs, events, and sub\-brands
* Serves as primary staff liaison to the destination marketing firm engaged by GEDP and the City of Easton, providing institutional knowledge, content, and quality oversight
* Develops and stewards GEDP's brand standards, tone of voice, and messaging architecture across all channels, programs, and audiences — including GEDP\-wide communications, the Easton Public Market, the Easton Farmers' Market, and other program\-specific presences
* Champions GEDP's commitment to design that is intentional, human, and rooted — actively resisting generic, corporate, or AI\-inflated visual and written output across all organizational materials
* Articulates GEDP's and Easton's identity — as a destination, a community, and a civic model — in language and images that resonate with residents, visitors, investors, and funders

**Creative Direction \& Team Leadership**

* Provides active, hands\-on art direction to the Lead Designer — not approval of finished work, but engagement in the creative process: reviewing concepts, pushing quality, ensuring visual output reflects GEDP's brand sensibility and the handmade, craft\-influenced aesthetic the organization values
* Provides editorial direction to the Content \& Social Media Manager across all content channels — setting voice, approving strategy, reviewing key content, and ensuring the work reflects organizational priorities and brand standards
* Directly supervises both direct reports; provides clear expectations, regular feedback, professional development support, and active workload management
* Implements, maintains, and enforces GEDP's marketing intake and triage process to ensure requests from programs and events staff are captured, triaged, assigned, and executed with appropriate lead time and quality oversight.
* Establishes and sustains the operational systems the function depends on — project management workflows in Monday.com, content calendars, creative asset libraries, and platform administration — and ensures they are consistently used across the organization, not merely designed and documented
* Manages the marketing and communications budget with discipline and transparency; makes vendor and platform decisions in collaboration with the Executive Director

**Capital Campaign \& Advancement Communications**

* In partnership with the Executive Director, Deputy Executive Director, and fundraising counsel, develops the case for support, campaign narrative, and donor\-facing materials for GEDP's capital campaign
* Drafts and edits grant proposals, reports, and funder communications that are accurate, compelling, and consistent with GEDP's brand voice
* Supports sponsorship outreach materials and corporate partnership communications in coordination with Sponsor Relations staff
* Develops communications strategy for major organizational announcements, capital project milestones, and institutional moments

**Editorial \& Content Oversight**

* Sets the editorial direction and content strategy across GEDP's channels — website, email, social media, print, and press — with a clear sense of audience, purpose, and voice for each
* Oversees GEDP's full content ecosystem, including program\-specific channels for the Easton Public Market, Easton Farmers' Market, West Ward Community Initiative, Easton Garden Works, and other programs; provides strategic guidance and brand stewardship to program staff managing those channels
* Reviews and edits high\-stakes content across the organization (press releases, Business Bugler copy, executive communications, major announcements, grant narratives)
* Develops, implements, and maintains a content calendar and production workflow that ensures marketing supports events and programs proactively, not reactively
* Oversees GEDP's direct communications platforms, including SMS and email marketing tools, ensuring they are maintained, operational, and deployed strategically

jobs.title: Executive Director Payor Relationships
jobs.description:
**Join a Team That Changes Lives**  

For more than 170 years, Elwyn has been leading the way in supporting children, teens, and adults with autism, intellectual and developmental disabilities, and behavioral health challenges. As a mission\-driven nonprofit, we’re here to create real change – helping people lead meaningful, fulfilling lives.  

Now, we’re looking for passionate team members to join us. Here, your work will change lives – including your own. You’ll make an impact every day, find purpose in what you do, and grow in a career that truly matters.  

At Elwyn, we take care of you while you care for others. We offer:* Generous Paid Time Off
* Comprehensive Medical/Dental/Vision Benefit Packages
* Earned Wage Access/On\-Demand Pay
* Paid On\-the\-Job Training
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Career Advancement Opportunities and Growth
* Flexible Schedules
* Retirement Savings Plan

 **Join us and be a part of something bigger. Apply today.**  

The **Executive Director of Payer Relationships** serves as Elwyn's senior leader responsible for developing, managing, and expanding strategic relationships with commercial, government, and value\-based payers across all operating states. This executive partners closely with organizational leadership to strengthen Elwyn's payer network, negotiate favorable reimbursement agreements, identify new contracting opportunities, and position Elwyn for long\-term growth.
  

  

This position combines executive relationship management, strategic contracting, reimbursement negotiation, and market expansion while overseeing the operational execution of payer agreements through the organization's contract management processes.
  

  

The Executive Director serves as the organization's primary liaison with health plans and accountable care organizations, ensuring payer strategies align with Elwyn's strategic growth priorities
  

  

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES*** Strategic \& Payor Development
* Develop and execute Elwyn's enterprise payer strategy across all markets.
* Identify opportunities to establish relationships with new commercial, Medicaid Managed Care, Medicare

Advantage, Behavioral Health Organizations, Accountable Care Organizations (ACOs), and other strategic payer partners.* Cultivate executive\-level relationships with payer leadership.
* In collaboration with the VP Marketing \& Growth, COO, and Service Line Leadership, represent Elwyn during executive payer meetings, negotiations, and strategic planning discussions.
* Identify emerging reimbursement opportunities that support organizational growth.
* Contract Negotiation \& Network Strategy
* Lead negotiations for new payer agreements and contract renewals.
* Negotiate reimbursement rates, value\-based payment arrangements, performance incentives, and contract language.
* Analyze reimbursement methodologies and financial impact of proposed agreements.
* Collaborate with Finance, Revenue Cycle, Legal, Program Operations, and Compliance throughout negotiations.
* Recommend contracting strategies that improve revenue while expanding market access.
* Maintain awareness of state and national payer trends impacting behavioral health and intellectual/developmental disability services.
* Relationship Management
* Serve as the executive relationship owner for Elwyn's largest payer partners.
* Conduct regular executive business reviews with health plans.
* Resolve high\-level payer issues affecting reimbursement, authorization, referrals, or operational performance.
* Partner with Business Development and Operations to strengthen referral pipelines from payer organizations.
* Develop collaborative initiatives that improve member outcomes and payer satisfaction.
* Contract Administration Oversight
* Provide leadership and oversight of the Contracting Coordinator responsible for contract administration.
* Ensure all contracts are routed, reviewed, approved, and executed through IntelAgree in accordance with organizational policies.
* Monitor contract lifecycle management including renewals, amendments, expirations, and compliance.
* Establish standardized contracting workflows across the organization.
* Maintain contract repository integrity and reporting.
* Credentialing, Provider Enrollment, and Insurance Paneling
* Provide executive oversight of organizational credentialing, provider enrollment, recredentialing, and insurance paneling activities.
* Ensure eligible practitioners, programs, facilities, and organizational entities are enrolled with appropriate government and commercial payers.
* Oversee processes involving CAQH, Medicare enrollment, Medicaid enrollment, commercial insurance

applications, delegated credentialing, roster management, and payer revalidation requirements.* Establish standards and performance expectations for timely provider enrollment and panel participation.
* Monitor enrollment status, application aging, payer response times, expiring credentials, recredentialing deadlines, and outstanding documentation.
* Ensure credentialing and enrollment activities support organizational compliance, billing readiness, and timely claims submission.
* Collaborate with Human Resources, Medical Staff Leadership, Compliance, Revenue Cycle, and Operations to obtain and maintain required provider information.
* Develop escalation processes for delayed enrollment, payer denials, closed panels, roster discrepancies, and other barriers to reimbursement.
* Ensure credentialing and paneling priorities align with program openings, service expansions, acquisitions, and new contract implementation.
* Market Intelligence
* Monitor payer market dynamics and competitive reimbursement trends.
* Evaluate opportunities for participation in innovative payment models including:
* Value\-Based Care, Risk\-Based Contracts, Alternative Payment Models, Behavioral Health Integration, Specialty Networks
* Provide executive leadership with recommendations regarding payer opportunities and threats.

jobs.title: Director of Development and Communications
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Black Chamber of Memphis seeks a strategic, relationship\-oriented **Director of Development and Communications** to lead the Chamber's fundraising, membership development, communications, and external engagement efforts.

Reporting directly to the **Chief Operating Officer (COO)** and serving as a member of the Chamber's leadership team, the Director will develop and execute an integrated strategy to expand the resources, relationships, membership, and visibility necessary to advance the Chamber's mission and strategic priorities.

The Director will lead efforts to strengthen relationships with corporations, foundations, government partners, members, sponsors, and other stakeholders while ensuring that the Chamber communicates a clear and consistent story about its mission, programs, accomplishments, and impact.

The Director will supervise the Membership Specialist and Website Designer/Social Media Coordinator and will work closely with the COO, President \& CEO, Chamber staff, Board members, and external partners.

Key ResponsibilitiesDevelopment and Fundraising

· Develop and execute an annual development strategy aligned with the Chamber's strategic priorities and financial goals.

· Build and manage a diversified portfolio of corporate, foundation, sponsorship, grant, and individual funding opportunities.

· Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward relationships with current and prospective funders, corporate partners, and sponsors.

· Develop sponsorship strategies and packages for Chamber programs, events, initiatives, and special projects.

· Coordinate grant development, including prospect research, proposal development, submission schedules, reporting requirements, and funder stewardship.

· Maintain a development pipeline and provide the COO with regular forecasts and reports on prospects, proposals, commitments, and revenue.

· Support the COO, President \& CEO, and Board members in major donor, corporate, and institutional relationship development.

Membership Development and Engagement

· Provide strategic leadership for membership recruitment, engagement, retention, and renewal.

· Supervise the Membership Specialist and establish measurable membership growth and retention goals.

· Develop strategies that strengthen the value proposition of Chamber membership and deepen member engagement.

· Use membership data and feedback to identify trends, opportunities, and areas requiring additional attention.

· Coordinate membership campaigns with the Chamber's broader communications, programming, events, and development activities.

· Strengthen pathways that move businesses from initial engagement with the Chamber to active membership, leadership, sponsorship, and long\-term investment.

Communications and Brand Management

· Develop and implement an integrated communications strategy that advances the Chamber's mission, programs, strategic priorities, and public profile.

· Ensure consistent messaging and brand standards across the Chamber's website, social media, newsletters, presentations, publications, events, and other communications.

· Supervise the Website Designer/Social Media Coordinator and establish priorities, content calendars, performance expectations, and measures of engagement.

· Develop compelling stories demonstrating the impact of Chamber members, programs, partnerships, and investments.

· Coordinate media relations, press releases, public announcements, executive communications, and other external communications.

· Support the COO and President \& CEO in developing speeches, presentations, talking points, reports, and other executive communications.

· Monitor communications analytics and use performance data to improve audience reach and engagement.

Corporate and Community Relations

· Develop and maintain strong relationships with corporations, foundations, government agencies, community organizations, economic development partners, and other stakeholders.

· Represent the Chamber at meetings, events, conferences, and community activities as appropriate.

· Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships that increase resources, expand services to members, or advance the Chamber's mission.

· Coordinate external engagement activities across development, membership, communications, and Chamber programming.

Leadership and Management

· Serve as a member of the Chamber's leadership team and contribute to organizational strategy, planning, budgeting, and performance management.

· Supervise, coach, and evaluate assigned staff and establish clear goals, priorities, and accountability measures.

· Build coordinated workflows across development, membership, communications, events, and programs.

· Develop annual departmental goals, work plans, budgets, and performance measures.

· Establish systems for tracking development activity, membership engagement, communications performance, and external relationships.

· Provide regular reports to the COO and, when appropriate, the President \& CEO and Board of Directors.

· Perform other leadership responsibilities consistent with the needs of a growing organization.

Performance Priorities

Success in this position will be measured by the Director's ability to:

· Increase and diversify contributed and sponsorship revenue.

· Build and maintain a strong pipeline of corporate, foundation, and institutional partners.

· Increase Chamber membership and improve member retention and engagement.

· Strengthen the Chamber's visibility, reputation, and consistency of communications.

· Improve coordination among fundraising, membership, communications, programs, and events.

· Develop effective staff members and establish clear systems of accountability.

· Demonstrate and communicate the measurable impact of the Chamber's work.

· Bachelor's degree in communications, marketing, business, nonprofit management, public administration, development, or a related field, or equi

jobs.title: Managing Director of Gift Planning
jobs.description:
Company Description  

  

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world\-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.


**Why join Harvard Medical School?**


Harvard Medical School's mission is to nurture a diverse, inclusive community dedicated to alleviating suffering and improving health and well\-being for all through excellence in teaching and learning, discovery and scholarship, and service and leadership.


You’ll be at the heart of biomedical discovery, education, and innovation, working alongside world\-renowned faculty and a community dedicated to improving human health. This is more than a job \- it’s an opportunity to shape the future of medicine.


**About the Office of Alumni Affairs and Development:**


The Office of Alumni Affairs and Development (AAD) at Harvard Medical School advances the School’s mission by inspiring philanthropy, fostering lifelong engagement, and building enduring partnerships with alumni, donors, volunteers, and friends around the world. Together, AAD professionals help secure the resources that fuel transformative biomedical research, educate future physician\-scientists and health care leaders, and accelerate discoveries that improve human health. Through a shared commitment to collaboration, innovation, integrity, and exceptional service, AAD creates meaningful opportunities for individuals to invest in Harvard Medical School’s vision and contribute to solutions for the world’s most pressing health challenges. **Executive Director**  

Conservation Voters for Idaho \| Salary Range: $110,000\-$120,000 \| Hybrid \- Boise, Idaho  

  

**The Opportunity**  

Conservation Voters for Idaho is looking for an accomplished, collaborative, and mission\-driven leader to serve as its next Executive Director.  

  

CVI protects Idaho’s environment and quality of life by informing, engaging, and empowering people who care about our natural heritage and healthy communities. Through CVI, CVIEF, and affiliated political action committees, the organization works to build political power for conservation and advance priorities that protect what makes Idaho special.  

  

This is an opportunity to lead an established and respected organization into its next chapter. CVI is looking for an Executive Director who knows that strong results start with strong people leadership and who can pair that with successful fundraising, strategic thinking, coalition\-building, and political judgment.  

  

The Executive Director will lead CVI, CVIEF, and affiliated political action committees, working in partnership with the appropriate Boards of Directors, senior leaders, staff, donors, funders, partners, and supporters to move the organizations' missions forward.  

  

**The Leader We Are Looking For**  

CVI's next Executive Director will be a proven organizational leader who builds trust, develops people, and creates the conditions for employees to do their best work.  

They will be collaborative, emotionally intelligent, adaptable, and approachable, while also being comfortable setting clear expectations, addressing difficult issues, making decisions, and holding people accountable.  

They will also be a strong relationship\-builder who is comfortable moving between conversations with staff, donors, funders, Board members, conservation partners, community leaders, elected officials, candidates, and other stakeholders.  

CVI operates in a complex political environment. The next Executive Director does not need to have spent their entire career in Idaho or in the conservation movement, but they do need the political judgment, relationship skills, and strategic thinking to build alliances and move conservation priorities forward.  

**Key Areas of Leadership*** **Lead People and Culture \-** Build and sustain a healthy, high\-performing workplace grounded in trust, respect, collaboration, accountability, and clear communication. Develop staff, provide meaningful feedback, be open and receptive to receiving feedback, address performance concerns, and support professional growth.
* **Provide Strategic and Political Leadership \-** Lead the work of CVI, CVIEF, and affiliated political action committees and guide effective political, advocacy, and electoral strategies that strengthen political power for conservation.
* **Drive Fundraising and Resource Development \-** Build strong relationships with donors, foundations, and institutional funders; take an active role in significant asks; secure financial support; and help diversify the organizations' funding base.
* **Build Relationships, Coalitions, and Partnerships \-** Develop productive relationships with conservation organizations, community partners, state and national partners, elected officials, candidates, supporters, and stakeholders across a range of political perspectives.
* **Partner with the Boards of Directors \-** Support effective governance through strong communication, strategic alignment, transparency, and organizational accountability.
* **Steward the Organization \-** Take responsibility for financial health, operational effectiveness, compliance, and long\-term sustainability.

**What You’ll Bring**  

Strong candidates will have senior or executive leadership experience in a nonprofit, mission\-driven, public\-sector, or similarly complex organization, along with a track record of leading and developing staff.  

They should also bring experience building trusted relationships, raising funds and developing resources, thinking strategically, communicating clearly, and making sound decisions, including when the issues are difficult.  

Experience with nonprofit executive leadership, Boards of Directors, coalition\-building, advocacy or electoral work, public policy, and environmental or conservation issues is highly valued. Familiarity with Idaho's political, nonprofit, conservation, or advocacy landscape is preferred.  

 CVI is also looking for a leader who demonstrates cultural competency and a commitment to racial equity, justice, and inclusive organizational practices.  

  

**Compensation \& Benefits**  

The salary range for the Executive Director is **$110,000\-$120,000**, depending on experience and qualifications.  

CVI offers a competitive benefits package, including employer\-paid employee premiums for health, dental, and vision insurance. Benefits also include a SIMPLE IRA with an employer match of up to 3%, flexible spending and dependent\-care accounts, a health reimbursement account, short\-term disability coverage, an Employee Assistance Program, and an annual cell\-phone reimbursement.  

CVI also offers generous paid time off, personal days, paid holidays, Summer Fridays between Memorial Day and Labor Day, a paid bonus week between Christmas and New Year's Day, sick leave, and additional paid leave benefits. Eligible employees may also qualify for a one\-month paid sabbatical after five years of continuous service.  

  

**Location \& Work Environment**  

CVI uses a hybrid work model, and the Executive Director is based in Boise, Idaho.
  

This role requires flexibility outside standard business hours. Periodic evening and weekend work should be expected for Board and organizational meetings, fundraising and community events, legislative and political activities, campaigns, and other mission\-related priorities.

NextUp RVA (NextUp) is a nonprofit organization powered by a network of providers and leaders with a shared commitment to ensuring youth have access to quality learning opportunities beyond the classroom. We are dedicated to making Out\-of\-School Time (OST) and expanded\-learning programs more accessible for youth, especially teenage youth. We do this by coordinating efforts and resources, knitting programs together into a cohesive system, helping individual programs function at a high level, and pushing the system to provide the greatest benefit to as many young people as possible.

**Position Summary**

The Vice President of Development (VP) is responsible for overseeing and managing the organization’s fundraising strategy, development, and execution. · Directs and leads adaptations to current strategies and practices in accordance with these changes and as necessary. Provides vision and direction to build and manage a full\-scale development program.

jobs.title: Senior Vice President of Development

Job Overview  
The Senior Vice President of Development (SVP of Development) provides executive leadership for e3 Partners Ministry’s comprehensive Development strategy and is accountable for the performance, sustainability, and growth of the organization’s broader philanthropic revenue portfolio.

Working closely with the Chief Executive Officer and Senior Leadership Team, the SVP establishes annual and long\-term revenue goals; develops fundraising strategies and forecasts; cultivates and solicits significant donors; strengthens donor retention and stewardship; expands and diversifies sources of philanthropic support; and leads the Development team, systems, and processes required to achieve organizational objectives.

The SVP leads an integrated fundraising program designed to generate both unrestricted and restricted support for e3’s mission, strategic priorities, initiatives, and long\-term ministry needs. The SVP serves as a member of the Senior Leadership Team and ensures that all fundraising activities are ethical, legal, biblical, consistent with e3 policies and values, and aligned with applicable ECFA standards.

Duties

*Fundraising Strategy \& Revenue Leadership*

* Develop and lead a comprehensive annual and long\-term Development strategy aligned with e3’s mission, strategic plan, financial priorities, and ministry opportunities.
* Partner with the CEO and Finance leadership to establish annual Development revenue goals, growth targets, forecasts, and funding priorities.
* Maintain executive accountability for the broader Development revenue portfolio, including unrestricted and restricted giving, major gifts, special initiatives and campaigns, foundation and grant support, planned giving, and other appropriate philanthropic channels.
* Build and maintain a healthy fundraising pipeline and regularly evaluate revenue performance, donor trends, opportunities, risks, and progress toward established goals.
* Develop strategies to strengthen and diversify philanthropic revenue, reduce concentration risk, expand the donor base, and increase long\-term financial sustainability.
* Oversee Development plans, departmental budgets, systems, resources, priorities, and performance measures.

*Major Donor Development \& Stewardship*

* Personally manage a portfolio of significant current and prospective donors and actively cultivate, solicit, and steward major and transformational gifts.
* Build long\-term, trust\-based relationships with individuals, families, foundations, churches, and other partners capable of making significant investments in e3’s mission.
* Lead efforts to expand the major\-gift pipeline and ensure an appropriate volume of meaningful donor proposals, asks, and follow\-up activities each year.
* Develop and oversee strategies for donor acquisition, engagement, retention, stewardship, reactivation, and increased giving.
* Ensure donors receive meaningful communication regarding ministry impact, outcomes, funding priorities, and the use of their gifts.
* Represent e3 Partners Ministry and its initiatives at donor meetings, ministry gatherings, events, conferences, and other external functions.

*Development Team Leadership*

* Provide leadership, strategic direction, coaching, and accountability to the Development team and its leaders.
* Establish clear departmental and individual goals, performance measures, portfolio expectations, priorities, and standards of excellence.
* Recruit, develop, retain, mentor, and appropriately structure a high\-performing Development team capable of supporting current and future organizational needs.
* Create a culture of collaboration, accountability, donor service, continuous improvement, and results\-oriented ministry.
* Maintain appropriate visibility into Development portfolios, pipelines, activities, and results while empowering team members to execute effectively.
* Address performance issues promptly and constructively and develop succession and talent strategies for the Development function.

*Development Operations, Reporting \& Organizational Collaboration*

* Ensure fundraising systems, CRM practices, donor records, prospect research, reporting, portfolio management, and Development data support effective donor engagement and sound decision\-making.
* Establish and monitor key Development metrics, dashboards, forecasts, and reports, and regularly communicate performance and recommendations to the CEO and Senior Leadership Team

**ABOUT ONEQUEST HEALTH** 

OneQuest Health is a leading behavioral health organization committed to transforming America’s health through compassionate, evidence based mental health services. Formerly Children’s Home of Northern Kentucky, the organization provides a wide continuum of care including outpatient therapy, medication management, partial hospitalization, targeted case management, and intensive outpatient programs tailored to the unique needs of children, teens, and adults.

With treatment available in offices, homes, schools, and via Telehealth, OneQuest Health meets clients where they are, removing barriers and expanding access to care. The organization is deeply committed to creating an inclusive, innovative, and welcoming environment for all identities, earning the All Children — All Families distinction for its leadership in supporting LGBTQ youth.

Grounded in evidence\-based practices and a client\-centered approach, OneQuest Health consistently delivers meaningful outcomes. We are the first organization in the Commonwealth of Kentucky to have achieved certification in the international Sanctuary Model, a model that serves as a blueprint for clinical and organization change through the promotion of safety and recovery from adversity through the active creation of a trauma\-informed community.

The organization’s culture is collaborative, mission\-driven, and rooted in compassion \-\- ensuring every individual has a clear path toward improved mental and emotional wellness. One Quest Health was one of the first organizations in Kentucky to utilize the Sanctuary Model, a trauma\-informed framework that helps healthcare organizations create a culture of safety, healing, and resilience by changing how staff, leaders, and patients interact across the entire system.

OneQuest Health is a dynamic, innovative employer intent on improving the lives of its clients and improving the communities in which those clients live with belief that a healthy community is key to having healthy families.

**Company Description**  

Habitat for Humanity of Forsyth County, established in 1985 on Christian principles, is dedicated to a vision where everyone has a decent place to live. The organization’s motivation is to unite people around the concept of “putting God’s love into action” along with others who are interested in helping those in need of improved shelter. Habitat Forsyth is an affiliate member of Habitat for Humanity International, founded in 1976\.


The Habitat model assists local hard\-working families who do not qualify for traditional mortgages to become homeowners. After meeting certain income, credit and rental history qualifications, future Habitat homeowners attend financial education and home ownership/maintenance classes. They earn 300 to 400 social engagement or “sweat equity” hours by helping build or remodel their own homes or those of others, and serve as volunteers with Habitat or in the community. Upon closing on the home, they begin paying an affordable mortgage back to Habitat, which allows the organization to help more families.


Volunteers play a crucial role in the success of Habitat Forsyth. Houses are built and remodeled largely with volunteer labor, enabling Habitat homeowner families to purchase decent, quality housing at an affordable price. Volunteers provide essential staffing at the three local ReStores, which serve as nonprofit home improvement stores and donation centers. Proceeds from the Habitat ReStores help support Habitat for Humanity’s mission of building or improving homes locally and around the world.


Habitat Forsyth has grown from $2\.8 million in revenue in FY17 to $6\.1 million in FY 25 and has built $11\.3 million in net assets. More than 350 families have found permanent homes since 1985*;* since the program’s founding in 2012, over 450families, veterans, and older adults have received home repairs through Habitat Forsyth.

The affordable housing challenges facing Forsyth County and North Carolina have never been greater. Rising housing costs, limited inventory, increasing construction expenses, barriers to homeownership, and growing housing insecurity among families, older adults, individuals with disabilities, and other vulnerable populations require bold leadership and innovative solutions.


The next Executive Director will inherit an organization with a respected mission, strong community recognition, dedicated supporters, and significant potential. At the same time, the organization faces important opportunities to strengthen internal operations, enhance organizational culture, develop staff capacity, deepen community partnerships, and expand its role as a leader in affordable housing development.


This is an opportunity for a mission\-driven executive who is energized by challenge, skilled at leading change, and excited about building both people and programs. The successful candidate will possess the strategic mindset of a chief executive, the operational discipline of a business leader, and the relationship\-building skills necessary to unite stakeholders around a shared vision for affordable housing in Forsyth County.

**The Leadership Challenge**


The Board of Directors is seeking a leader who embraces complexity and can successfully navigate both organizational and community challenges while positioning Habitat Forsyth for long\-term impact and sustainability.


Key opportunities for the next Executive Director include:

* Expanding Habitat Forsyth's housing development capabilities beyond traditional individual home construction toward larger\-scale affordable housing and neighborhood development initiatives.
* Strengthening partnerships with municipalities, financial institutions, developers, employers, philanthropic organizations, and community stakeholders.
* Navigating the increasingly complex affordable housing environment in North Carolina, including public funding opportunities, regulatory requirements, development challenges, and housing finance mechanisms.
* Enhancing Habitat Forsyth's reputation as a trusted, influential, and collaborative community leader focused on housing solutions.
* Ensuring long\-term organizational sustainability through sound financial management, strategic growth, diversified funding sources, and staff development.


This role requires a leader who is equally comfortable inspiring employees, cultivating donors, negotiating development opportunities, engaging public officials, and representing Habitat Forsyth throughout the community.

**The Position**


The Executive Director serves as the chief executive of Habitat for Humanity of Forsyth County and is responsible for overall leadership, management, strategic direction, financial stewardship, and public representation of the organization.


Working closely with the Board of Directors, staff, volunteers, donors, government leaders, community partners, and Habitat for Humanity International, the Executive Director will develop and execute a vision that strengthens organizational effectiveness while expanding Habitat's ability to address affordable housing needs throughout Forsyth County.


The Executive Director must be a visible, stable, and respected community leader who inspires confidence, communicates effectively across diverse audiences, and builds strong relationships both internally and externally. The successful candidate will bring a calm, steady leadership style, sound judgment, and emotional intelligence.

**MISSION:** Optimize the health, development, education, and well\-being of babies, toddlers, and preschoolers through a family\-driven, equitable, community\-based system of high\-quality prenatal and early childhood programs and services.
  
  

The Early Childhood Education and Care Department was established on July 1, 2020\. The Department's aim is to create a more cohesive, equitable, and effective early childhood system in New Mexico. That means coordinating a continuum of programs from prenatal to five\-and ensuring that families in every corner of the state can access the services they need.
  
  

This posting will be used for ongoing recruitment and may close at any time. Applicant lists may be screened more than once.
  
Why does the job exist?
  
  

This position exists to safeguard the financial integrity of the Early Childhood Education and Care Department (ECECD) by establishing and maintaining a strong, reliable internal control framework and ensuring complete, timely, and accurate financial reporting across all state and federal funding streams. As a core steward of public resources, the role provides the leadership necessary to oversee federal and state reporting requirements, ensure compliance with model accounting practices and statutory obligations, and guide the department's budget development, fiscal planning, and cash management activities. By embedding accountability, transparency, and sound financial practices throughout the agency, this position enables ECECD to operate effectively, meet audit and regulatory expectations, and strategically deploy funds in support of New Mexico's early childhood system.
  
How does it get done?
  
  

The Deputy Director of Finance serves as the strategic and operational lead for all financial activities within the Administrative Services Division of the Early Childhood Education and Care Department. This role ensures the integrity of fiscal operations by overseeing internal controls, budgetary systems, and accounting frameworks. The position manages complex and moderately complex budget initiatives in compliance with state and federal laws and ensures adherence to the Model Accounting Practices established by the Department of Finance and Administration.
  
  

As a key advisor to senior leadership, the Deputy Director develops strategic financial plans, performance metrics, and continuous improvement initiatives. The role ensures timely and accurate reporting, audits, and vendor payments, while certifying that all expenditures are necessary, publicly beneficial, and legally compliant. The Deputy Director also leads a multidisciplinary team, coordinates cross­\-divisional support, and communicates fiscal policies to internal and external stakeholders.

We are seeking a passionate and dynamic Executive Director to lead our Camp Ministries, inspiring youth and fostering a vibrant community rooted in faith, growth, and service.
