EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR: CAMPING AND RETREAT MINISTRIES

The New York Annual Conference of the United Methodist Church is seeking a full\-time Executive Director of our Camping and Retreat Ministries.

The Executive Director of Camping and Retreat Ministries (“CRM”) is the on\-site Director of Quinipet Camp and Retreat Center, a year\-round facility on Shelter Island, NY with oversight and support for Kingswood Campsite, a seasonal campsite in Hancock, NY. The CRM provides a sacred space apart from the everyday world where all are welcomed to experience God’s creation. CRM encourages Christian community and spiritual growth through overnight summer camp and year round retreats, and works to develop and nurture the leaders of tomorrow. The Executive Director guides staff and volunteers in partnership with the Camps Governing Board to accomplish overall goals.

Principal Duties and Tasks include: Oversight of two locations in New York state; administration and management of regular and seasonal staff, and budgets and financial records; maintenance and management of properties and facilities; marketing to and recruitment of clientele and staff; development of long term goals for expansion of all programs; maintain risk and regulatory government and UMC standards; attendance and participation in monthly Governing Board and Task Force meetings, and New York Annual Conference meeting in June.

Applicants must possess a Bachelor’s Degree (Master’s degree preferred) and have at least 5\-10 years of experience in managing a Christian camping environment or related experience. Member of a United Methodist Church (preferred) or possess significant understanding of UM doctrine and polity. Commitment to working in a Christian environment. Acceptance of and ability to communicate with people of various religious affiliations, ethnicities, genders, ages, and differing abilities is vitally important. Excellent computer skills, including working knowledge of QuickBooks. Experience with CampMinder and Gazebo registration systems is a plus. Must agree to live on\-site, year\-round at Camp Quinipet, on Shelter Island, NY. Some travel within New York Annual Conference area is expected.

A three bedroom, two bath, 1400 sq. ft. house and basic utilities are included in the compensation package, which also includes health insurance, pension, and other employee benefits.

To learn more about the New York Annual Conference please visit us at: www.nyac.com

To apply, please send a cover letter, resume

* Oversee the planning and execution of diverse youth programs including outdoor activities, arts, theater experiences, tutoring sessions, and youth group activities.
* Ensure compliance with all safety protocols including first aid procedures, CPR/AED operation, behavior management policies, and child supervision standards.
* Manage daily camp operations such as scheduling activities, maintaining facilities, coordinating transportation, and overseeing outdoor work environments.
* Cultivate positive relationships with campers’ families and community partners to enhance program outreach and support.
* Promote a safe environment by implementing child protection policies, conducting regular safety drills, and maintaining accurate records of incidents or emergencies.

**Experience**

* Proven experience working with children in educational or recreational settings; prior camp experience is highly preferred.
* Demonstrated leadership in youth development programs or similar roles involving team supervision and program management.
* Strong background in classroom management, behavior management strategies, and childhood development principles.
* Certification in first aid, CPR/AED operation (including AED), child safety protocols, and relevant certifications in special education or Christian counseling are highly desirable.
* Experience facilitating youth group activities or theater\-based programs that promote creativity and teamwork.

* Excellent communication skills with the ability to motivate staff and connect effectively with children of diverse backgrounds.

Join us to lead a vibrant ministry that transforms lives through faith\-based programming! We’re committed to empowering our team members with the tools they need to succeed while creating memorable experiences for every camper.

jobs.description:
**Join the Oregon Symphony Team as our Director of Development, Planned and Major Gifts!**


As our Director of Development, Planned and Major Gifts, you will help shape the future of the Oregon Symphony by building meaningful relationships with donors whose generosity sustains our mission for generations to come. Through strategic major gift fundraising, planned giving, and thoughtful donor stewardship, you'll play a key role in advancing philanthropic support and strengthening the Symphony's long\-term financial future. Here's how you'll make a difference:


* Build and manage a portfolio of major and planned giving donors and prospects, developing meaningful relationships that inspire transformational philanthropy.
* Develop and execute individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies that align donor passions with the Symphony's mission.
* Lead the Oregon Symphony's planned giving program, expanding legacy giving opportunities and encouraging long\-term philanthropic investment.
* Prepare compelling major, blended, and planned gift proposals that help donors achieve their charitable goals while advancing organizational priorities.
* Partner with the Vice President of Development, Board members, and fellow fundraisers to cultivate and solicit high\-capacity donors.
* Mentor Development team members on planned giving strategies and emerging gift opportunities, strengthening fundraising capacity across the department.
* Create planned giving materials and donor communications that clearly communicate the impact of philanthropy.
* Represent the Symphony at donor meetings, concerts, cultivation events, and community gatherings, building lasting relationships with supporters.
* Monitor portfolio performance, donor activity, and fundraising progress to help achieve annual and long\-term revenue goals.

This role is pivotal in helping ensure the Oregon Symphony's artistic excellence continues to flourish for generations to come. If you're passionate about building lasting donor relationships and creating meaningful philanthropic partnerships, we'd love to have you on the team.

  


**Qualifications:**


* Bachelor's degree and at least five years of fundraising experience with a focus on major and planned gifts, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Minimum of one year of direct planned giving experience.
* Demonstrated success securing major and planned gifts and managing donor portfolios.
* Strong understanding of planned giving strategies and donor\-centered fundraising.
* Excellent communication, relationship\-building, and organizational skills.
* Experience with donor CRM systems; Tessitura experience strongly preferred.
* Collaborative leadership style with a passion for mentoring colleagues and advancing organizational fundraising goals.

**We Offer:**


* A chance to be part of a respected and mission\-driven organization.
* A collaborative Development team focused on building meaningful donor relationships and lasting community impact.
* An opportunity to help shape the future of one of the nation's leading orchestras through transformational philanthropy.

**Status and Compensation:**


This is a full\-time, exempt position currently following a hybrid work model with 2\-3 days per week in the office. Regular evening and weekend attendance at donor events, concerts, and cultivation activities is expected.


**Salary Range:** $95\-100k


**Benefits:** Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, long\-term disability insurance, and retirement plan.


**How to Apply:**


If you're ready to help inspire transformational philanthropy and build lasting relationships that support the future of the Oregon Symphony, we'd love to hear from you. **Please submit a cover letter and resume to careers@orsymphony.org** with the job title in the subject line.  

  



The Oregon Symphony is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, or national origin. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

jobs.title: Associate Director of Development
jobs.description:
### **What We Can Achieve Together:**

  

The Associate Director of Development (ADoD) is an experienced “out the door” fundraiser and self\-starter with excellent writing skills who excels as a collaborative team member who brings leadership to their portfolio and fundraising strategies. The ADoD develops, implements, and plans for the cultivation and solicitation of gift prospects, primarily individual donors and potential corporate, foundation, and institutional funders. This person will be part of a team that is driven, strategic and thoughtful. This role is ideal for a strategic fundraiser who enjoys identifying, qualifying, and building relationships with new major donor prospects while also managing a portfolio of established donors to contribute to the ongoing mission of our global conservation work.  



  

### **We’re Looking for You:**

  

The Associate Director of Development for The Nature Conservancy in Maine is based out of our Brunswick, Maine office and is responsible for managing a portfolio of qualified donors and for building strong relationships. The ADoD promotes a culture of philanthropy among their peers and volunteers and works closely with the development team, Advisory Board of Trustees, natural partners, and other Conservancy staff to determine effective strategies for engaging identified donors and prospects and deepening their relationships with The Nature Conservancy. This person inspires by telling stories about the Conservancy’s work and ably connects donors to their values.  



The ADoD understands and applies complex principles of developing donor strategies and builds strong relationships with a portfolio of prospects, as well as new and current donors. They are an experienced, creative and strategic fundraiser driven by donor interest and energized by pipeline discovery and qualification. The successful candidate will be highly collaborative and bring a track record of delivering results. As part of a 9\-person team, this role focuses largely on discovery and qualification towards building a high\-value portfolio. They are responsible for direct asks for both global and local Conservancy priorities to meet funding needs. They discuss assets proficiently and listen for opportunities for gifts of assets or other non\-cash gifts, such as planned gifts and gifts of real estate or trade lands. They incorporate blended gifts and gifts of assets in proposals to donors. They understand organizational budgets and are proficient in utilizing this knowledge to build proposal budgets. They will work collaboratively across chapters and programs with a spirit of “One Conservancy” and leverage institutional knowledge and networks for successful and sophisticated donor strategies. They work closely with chapter leadership (including the State Director and Director of Conservation) and manage assigned trustee relationships and/or volunteer engagement. jobs.title: Director of Fundraising / Development
jobs.description:
**Type:** Full\-time contractor (hours negotiable)

**Location:** Remote, based in the SF Bay Area, Seattle, New York, or Washington, DC (US time zones)

**Travel:** Expectation of 20\-40% travel time between US, EU and India.


OpenFn is the Digital Public Good for public service automation \& AI orchestration. Our platform automates data exchange and digital workflows so that governments and NGOs can deliver public services more efficiently, achieve interoperability across fragmented systems, and scale critical public services across health, humanitarian, and government programs.


Our team, Open Function Group, the primary steward of this open\-source platform, is a lean, fully\-remote team of integration specialists, solution architects, and implementation consultants working across 15\+ countries.


We are not making marginal improvements to already comfortable lives. We are building the digital public infrastructure that allows governments to function, clinics to operate, and vulnerable populations to access services they depend on.


Supporting document (with ideas for fundraising against): https://www.openfn.org/blog/dpi\-ai


The role**We're hiring OpenFn's first Director of Fundraising to lead our organization’s fundraising efforts with major donors, foundations, and mission\-aligned funders who invest in Digital Public Goods, Digital Public Infrastructure, and social\-impact technology. We will always act in the public interest, never for private profit. We want investment which is aligned as such.**


To date, OpenFn's growth has come from delivering complex digital transformation and implementation projects, and from fundraising efforts our CEO has largely driven himself. As we invest more deliberately in philanthropic and institutional funding to complement our subscription revenue, we're looking for an experienced fundraiser to build this function from the ground up: developing a fundraising strategy, cultivating and stewarding relationships with foundations and major donors, and helping OpenFn secure the multi\-year support it needs to keep expanding access to public service automation.


You already have a network of relationships with foundations, funders, and philanthropists active in international development, Digital Public Goods, and technology for social good, and you know how to translate a mission into a compelling case for support. You're comfortable being both the strategist and the one making the ask: this is a foundational hire, so you'll build the playbook as you go rather than inherit one.


We believe some of OpenFn's biggest fundraising opportunities sit at the intersection of philanthropy and policy, for instance helping governments understand why workflow and AI orchestration are essential to resilient digital public infrastructure or articulating the influence that open platforms have on the concentration of power in a market. Prior experience in policy conversations around Digital Public Goods or ICT for Development, and a passion for understanding and addressing the macroeconomic forces that shape wealth inequality is a requirement.


What you'll be doing**Build our fundraising strategy**

* Develop and lead OpenFn's fundraising strategy across major donors, foundations, and other mission\-aligned funders
* Establish the processes, systems, and reporting cadence a growing fundraising function needs, since you will be OpenFn's first dedicated fundraising hire (see helpful pointers from Wayan Vota!)
* Set and track fundraising priorities in partnership with the CEO and leadership team

**Cultivate \& grow major donor and foundation relationships**

* Identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with foundations, family offices, and individual major donors aligned with OpenFn's mission
* Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective funders, from first conversation through multi\-year commitment
* Represent OpenFn credibly and persuasively with senior funder audiences, translating our technical work into a compelling case for impact and support

**Develop compelling funding proposals \& materials**

* Write and coordinate proposals, funding narratives, and reports that clearly connect OpenFn's work to funder priorities
* Partner with the CEO and program teams to gather the impact data and stories that anchor a strong case for support

**Engage the policy \& DPG ecosystem (a plus)**

* Build relationships across the broader Digital Public Goods and Digital Public Infrastructure funding community
* Represent OpenFn in relevant policy conversations and convenings where doing so could unlock new funding relationships

**Report on progress \& sustain funder relationships**

* Track and report on fundraising pipeline, commitments, and funder engagement to the CEO and leadership
* Ensure funders receive timely, high\-quality communications and reporting that keeps them engaged for the long term

  

**Requirements**  

  

Required Qualifications* 10\+ years of experience in fundraising, development, or philanthropic partnerships, ideally within international development, global health, or technology\-for\-good organizations
* A demonstrated network of relationships with foundations, major donors, or other institutional funders active in social impact or technology for development
* A track record of securing significant gifts or grants and stewarding funder relationships over multiple years
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical, mission\-driven work into a compelling case for support for a range of audiences
* Strong project management and organizational skills, comfortable building process where none exists
* Ability to work independently and as part of a small, fully\-remote team
* Fluent, professional\-level English communication skills (written and verbal), with the ability to work effectively across a distributed, multicultural team
* Reliable access to a quiet, dedicated remote workspace with stron

Overview: **Our Commitment to Equity**  

The Y actively promotes a culture free from bias and injustice. We are dedicated to removing institutional and systemic barriers that result in oppression and racism. We will be accountable to marginalized communities for creating equitable and sustainable environments where social justice is woven into every facet of our programs, and by caring for our communities in a culturally versatile and respectful manner. **Job Summary**
As a member of the Financial Development Team, the Director of Philanthropy \- Community Giving will be responsible for creating the philanthropic strategy and objectives for community giving and direct the implementation in assigned Branches, Districts, Centers of Excellence (CoEs) or Departments. Responsibilities will include working with a portfolio of individuals based on assignment to acquire, cultivate, solicit, and steward community level gifts up to $10,000\. Responsible for a comprehensive and aggressive social media and in\-person campaign plan structure that will maximize annual giving as well as capital opportunities. This Director will lead the strategy to assist volunteer leadership, staff leaders and donors to develop a culture of philanthropy as a foundation of annual giving and springboard for major and planned giving programs. **Position Type/Expected Hours of Work**  

This is a full\-time position, working Monday through Friday with occasional nights and weekends as needed.  

Flexible Work, also called remote work or telecommuting, is a flexible work location arrangement that permits YGS employees to work at home, at a non\-office location, at a satellite office, a YGS facility or any of the above. In most cases, flexible work arrangements outline the workplace conditions of YGS employees who are approved to periodically work from their homes or another convenient location in the YGS area. **What you'll get from working at The Y:*** Membership to the YMCA of Greater Seattle for you and your household
* Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life insurance
* Retirement with generous employer contributions
* Free access to mental health resources
* Rapidly\-accruing paid time off (PTO)
* Discounts on qualifying YMCA of Greater Seattle childcare and day camp programs

* Support the Financial Development Team in meeting its annual fundraising targets ($11M\+) and capital fundraising objectives.
* Works collaboratively and strategically with the Branch Executives, Board Members, other fundraising professionals, volunteers, and other Y leaders to cultivate and solicit donors for association\-wide priorities.
* Serve as fundraising lead for assigned events, projects, activities, audiences, and areas of fundraising in assigned area (E.g. Annual Fund Drive, GiveBIG, planned giving, membership, etc.)
* Renew and rebuild relationships with prior donors who have been dormant in recent years, as assigned.
* Establish new donor relationships and expand pipeline, generate new leads, and qualify major gift prospects from research, prospect tracking tools, fundraising colleagues, and prior experience. Work with the Financial Development Team to identify and cultivate major prospects for future giving to annual, capital, program planned/legacy gifts, and endowment support.
* Develop appropriate cultivation strategies, including working with volunteers to move potential donors in an appropriate and timely fashion towards greater understand of the mission and impact of the assigned areas and toward solicitation.
* Make solicitations when appropriate.
* Provide leadership, coaching and training for select campaign committees, branch boards, and volunteers, including identifying and recruiting volunteers. Schedule and support campaign leadership meetings and ensure quality engagement and participation.
* Other duties as assigned.

 **Leadership Characteristics*** Seattle is known for its vibrant and diverse community across the private, public, and not\-for\-profit sectors. Working effectively across constituency groups including large and small businesses, not–for\-profit organizations, civic leaders, and the YGS staff, this individual will:
* Be a hands\-on, team\-oriented leader with highly developed interpersonal skills, proficient as an influencer and negotiator.
* Champion social responsibility, diversity, inclusion, justice and equity; model cultural competence and support diversity, effectively work with people of different backgrounds, abilities, opinions, and perceptions.
* Build and maintain ongoing partnerships with key stakeholders.
* Delegate and facilitate increased collaboration across the organization.
* Demonstrate strong and passionate leadership with the ability to effectively execute and adeptly work through political barriers, build consensus, and enact social change.
* Communicate vision for both the short\- and long\-term direction of the organization’s Branches, Districts, Centers of Excellence (CoEs) and Departments.
* Effectively manage people and develop their skills and abilities.
* Take the initiative and hold themselves and others accountable to meet or exceed quantitative and qualitative goals relating to people (employees and members), philanthropy, finance, and volunteerism.
* Maintain accountability by ensuring compliance with all regulations and laws, as well as the code of ethics for fundraising professionals.
* Nurture and develop a robust portfolio of prospects and donors along with key engagement tactics.

jobs.title: Director or Senior Director of Government Relations, New York State
jobs.description:
**Position Title:** Director or Senior Director of Government Relations, New York State


**Reports To:** Executive Vice President and Chief of Staff


**Direct Reports:**None


**Department:** External Affairs


**Location:** Albany, New York


**FLSA Status:** Exempt


**Salary Range:** $140,000 \- $190,000


**Date:** September 2026


**About the Open Space Institute**



The Open Space Institute (OSI) is a national leader in land conservation and efforts to make parks and other protected land more welcoming for all. Since 1974, OSI has partnered in the protection of more than 2\.5 million at\-risk and environmentally sensitive acres in the eastern U.S. OSI’s land protection promotes clean air and water, improves access to recreation, provides wildlife habitat, strengthens communities, and combats the devastating impacts of extreme weather.


**Position Summary**



This position serves as OSI’s lead strategist for New York State government relations, advancing state\-level policy, funding, advocacy, and agency engagement in support of OSI’s conservation mission. Reporting to the Executive Vice President and Chief of Staff, the role leads OSI’s efforts to strengthen conservation funding, build coalitions, inform policy through research and advocacy, and expand land protection and improve access to public land across New York State.



Working closely with colleagues across the organization, the position will serve as OSI’s primary representative to New York State government, cultivating senior\-level relationships with elected officials, agency leaders, and key partners to advance OSI’s policy objectives and strategic priorities.



The position will work across OSI departments, coalitions, and advocacy partners to align policy, funding, and program priorities. The ideal candidate will be a self\-directed strategist who excels in relationship\-building, influence, cross\-functional collaboration, and leadership.



While the position’s primary focus is New York State, it may also support related policy and government relations work in other eastern U.S. states where OSI has active conservation initiatives and partnerships.



This position may be filled at the Director or Senior Director level, depending on the selected candidate’s experience and qualifications.


**Primary Roles and Responsibilities**


**Government Relations and Policy Implementation**


* Lead the development and implementation of OSI’s state policy, advocacy, and public funding strategies in collaboration with executive leadership, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and long\-term conservation objectives.
* Oversee the tracking and analysis of New York State legislation, budget items, and regulatory initiatives related to conservation funding (e.g., Environmental Protection Fund), climate resilience, public lands, and outdoor recreation.
* Coordinate OSI’s representation with the Governor’s office, key state agencies, including DEC and OPRHP, and statewide coalitions addressing open space, parkland, and public access policies.
* Serve as OSI’s senior representative and spokesperson in meetings with legislators, administration and agency leaders, and coalition partners.
* Develop and deliver policy briefs, testimony, and correspondence articulating OSI’s positions to policymakers and partners.
* Lead planning and strategy for OSI’s participation in key lobbying days and advocacy events, including EPF Lobby Day and Parks and Public Lands Advocacy Day.
* Manage external consultants, lobbyists, and advocacy contracts to ensure alignment with OSI’s strategic priorities.
* Develop strategies to increase public investment in conservation, parks, greenways, and climate resilience initiatives, positioning OSI and its partners to pursue state funding opportunities.
* Identify emerging political, legislative, and funding opportunities and advise OSI leadership on strategic actions that advance the organization's mission and long\-term impact.


**Relationship\-Building, Outreach and Coalition Development**


* Expand, cultivate, and leverage high\-level relationships with state legislators, administration and agency leadership, and partner organizations to advance OSI’s policy and funding goals.
* Convene and lead statewide strategic coalitions with nonprofit, environmental, and community partners to shape advocacy efforts and agendas, mobilize partners and communities around key priorities, and strengthen statewide impact.
* Advise and collaborate with OSI program teams (Land, Parks, Stewardship, and External Affairs) on government\-related opportunities affecting land acquisitions, transfers, and stewardship.
* Represent OSI at public hearings, stakeholder meetings, ensuring a consistent and influential organizational presence.


**Communications and Public Engagement**


* Partner with OSI Communications leadership to develop and deliver messaging that advances OSI’s state policy priorities.
* Serve as one of OSI’s primary external leaders on policy and government relations matters, representing OSI with elected officials, agencies, coalition leaders, funders, and other stakeholders, acting as a policy spokesperson for OSI in public, media, and coalition forums.
* Prepare and review briefing materials, talking points, and presentations for OSI leadership and board members.
* Contribute to OSI’s thought leadership by articulating the organization’s role in advancing conservation and public access policy.


**Internal Coordination**


* Serve as a strategic advisor to OSI’s Executive Team, Board, and program leaders on public policy, government funding, and legislative matters, translating policy developments into actionable organizational strategies.
* Track and evaluate advocacy outcomes and report on progress to OSI leadership, funders, and the board.
* Lead cross\-functional policy initiatives that require coordination across multiple OSI teams and/or external partners; supervise staff or consultants supp

jobs.title: Director of Advancement Services and Annual Giving
jobs.description:
**INSTITUTIONAL OVERVIEW:** Logan University prepares health science students through evidence\-informed care, clinical excellence, and a holistic approach to health and wellness. Logan has led chiropractic education since 1935 and continues to broaden its academic offerings across the health sciences. The University is entering a new phase of institutional growth that calls for a mature, scalable advancement operation capable of supporting strategic priorities, student success, and long\-term financial sustainability.




**POSITION SUMMARY:** The Director of Advancement Services and Annual Giving carries dual responsibility for the infrastructure and the unrestricted revenue engine of Logan's advancement program. The position oversees all advancement services functions at the University — donor database administration, gift processing, gift accounting and compliance, reporting and analytics, prospect research, and planned giving records — and simultaneously holds direct revenue accountability for the annual fund.


This is a builder's role in a small, high\-expectation shop. As Logan scales annual philanthropic revenue from approximately $1 million to $4 million and above, this position supplies both the operating discipline that makes growth measurable and the annual giving pipeline that feeds it. The Director designs and executes the full annual giving program, carries a defined dollar and donor\-count goal, and is measured on results.


Reporting to the Chief Development Officer, the Director serves as the University's authority on advancement data and gift compliance, and as a trusted operational partner to Finance, Alumni Relations, Marketing, and Information Technology.




**PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**




**Annual Giving \& Revenue Responsibility:**

* Carry and achieve an annual fund revenue goal that will be determined after the Direct Mail is reestablished and the Annual Fund is stabilized, with accountability for dollars raised, donor count, donor retention rate, average gift, and cost to raise a dollar.
* Design, execute, and continuously improve a multi\-channel annual giving calendar spanning direct mail, email, digital and social, phone, giving day, employee and faculty/staff campaigns, student philanthropy, and year\-end appeals.
* Develop segmentation, case language, ask strings, and channel strategy by constituency, including alumni, current and former patients, parents, faculty and staff, corporate partners, and friends of the University.
* Own the full donor lifecycle for annual giving: acquisition, renewal, upgrade, reinstatement, and lapsed\-donor recapture, each with stated targets and post\-appeal analysis.
* Build and manage leadership annual giving society with recognition tiers set at $25,000\+, $10,000\+, $5,000\+, and $1,000\+, including tier\-specific cultivation and stewardship.
* Identify, qualify, and refer to annual fund donors demonstrating major gift capacity to the Chief Development Officer, and maintain the documented handoff process between annual and major giving.
* Manage annual giving vendors, production schedules, and program budget; negotiate and monitor vendor performance against cost and delivery standards.
* Report annual fund progress against goal to the Chief Development Officer monthly and to the Board of Trustees on the reporting cycle established by the Chief Development Officer.




**Database Administration \& Data Governance:**

* Serve as system owner and primary administrator for Raiser's Edge NXT in both Web View and Database View, including user provisioning, security groups, fund and campaign structure, attribute and code table governance, query and export libraries, and release management.
* Establish, document, and enforce University\-wide data entry standards, naming conventions, coding structures, and record\-retention practices.
* Own the integrity of constituent data, including duplicate resolution, address and deceased updates, NCOA processing, email and phone hygiene, and periodic data audits.
* Manage integrations and data flows between the donor database and Logan's finance system, student information system, online giving platform, email marketing platform, event registration, and wealth screening tools.
* Ensure donor data in electronic and paper form is secured, backed up, access\-controlled, and retained in line with University policy and professional standards.




**Gift Processing, Gift Accounting \& Compliance:**

* Manage the complete gift\-entry lifecycle so that all gifts are batched, entered, and deposited accurately and that acknowledgments are produced within five business days of receipt.
* Process and administer complex gift types, including pledges and pledge payments, recurring gifts, ACH and credit card transactions, matching gifts, securities, donor\-advised fund distributions, in\-kind gifts, and gifts of real and tangible property.
* Reconcile the donor database to the general ledger monthly with Finance, resolve variances, and serve as the advancement lead for annual audit requests.
* Ensure compliance with IRS substantiation and disclosure requirements, including quid pro quo disclosure and preparation of Forms 8283, 8282, and 1099\-R.
* Maintain and update the advancement policies and procedures manual, including the gift acceptance policy, counting and crediting standards consistent with CASE guidelines, and written desk procedures for every recurring process.




**Reporting, Analytics \& Performance Measurement:**

* Build and maintain performance dashboards and standing reports for the President, the Board of Trustees, the Chief Development Officer, and academic and administrative partners.
* Produce fiscal year\-to\-date revenue reporting aligned to Logan's September 1 through August 31 fiscal year, including comparison to prior year, goal, and forecast.

The Program Director, Community Supports – Private Duty provides strategic and operational leadership for Partners in Care Foundation’s Private Duty Services portfolio, including Respite, Personal Care, and Homemaker Services delivered through Medi\-Cal Community Supports, managed care contracts, and other funding sources.


Reporting to the Senior Director, Community Care Hub, the Program Director oversees program operations, provider network performance, health plan relationships, quality and compliance, financial performance, and sustainable growth while ensuring high\-quality, person\-centered service delivery.

* Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Social Work, Healthcare Administration, Gerontology, Business Administration, Nursing, or a related field.

JCC Association of North America is seeking an experienced, creative, and highly collaborative professional to join its Center for Talent Development as Program Director, Center for Talent Development. new_jobs.title: Executive Director, NWSL Foundation
new_jobs.description:
The National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) is one of the fastest\-growing professional sports leagues in the U.S., powered by 16 clubs and a deep roster of the world’s best players, and built on record\-shattering fan, media and commercial growth. Now in its 14th season, the league’s momentum continues to accelerate, with viewership and attendance numbers growing rapidly, social media fandom on the rise, team valuations massively increasing and new top sponsors investing in the NWSL brand. This unprecedented growth in audience, media reach, and franchise value reflects the NWSL’s expanding fan base and increasing dominance in the sports\-media landscape and popular culture.

  

The future of the NWSL is now — and we’re looking for world\-class talent like you to help us continue the momentum.

### **The Role**

**About the NWSL Foundation**


The NWSL Foundation exists to advance the health and longevity of women athletes by supporting women’s health research and convening and coordinating the women’s athletic health research ecosystem. The Foundation helps guide the research agenda to ensure critical questions are identified, research efforts are aligned across institutions, and findings are translated into practical insights and resources for the benefit of the public and women and girls who participate in athletics.


The Foundation’s role is not to replicate academic research or function primarily as a grantmaker. Instead, it serves as a field\-shaping platform—aligning researchers, practitioners, and funders; reducing redundancy; elevating rigor; ensuring practical application, and enabling research that meaningfully advances women athletes’ health, performance, and longevity.


Anchored by an initial endowment, the Foundation will operate with scientific independence, disciplined governance, and a clear focus on actionability.

**Role Overview**
=================


The Executive Director is the founding leader and public face of the NWSL Foundation. This role is accountable for setting and stewarding the research agenda, convening the ecosystem, and ensuring the Foundation earns credibility as a trusted leader in women's athletic health research.


The Executive Director is not expected to be a career researcher or a traditional frontline fundraiser. Instead, this role requires a leader who has worked closely with researchers, clinicians, funders, and institutional partners—and who understands what it takes to develop credible research agendas, synthesize complex information, and mobilize resources in service of impact.


The Executive Director must be equally comfortable engaging senior researchers and clinicians, league and club leadership, players, and donors. This role requires judgment, credibility, and the ability to direct complex, multi\-stakeholder conversations—not simply administer programs.


The Executive Director reports to the NWSL Foundation Board and partners closely with League leadership, including Sporting and High Performance, while preserving scientific independence.

### **What You Will Own \& Drive**


1\. Research Agenda Leadership \& Field Stewardship

* Own and steward the Foundation’s multi\-year research agenda, grounded in elite women athlete needs and informed by the global research landscape.
* Identify gaps, redundancies, and under\-resourced areas across women’s athletic health research.
* Guide prioritization of research questions to ensure relevance, rigor, and actionability.
* Serve as an authoritative voice in shaping norms, priorities, and standards across the field—drawing credibility from prior leadership experience at the intersection of research, sport, and institutions.


2\. Convening \& Ecosystem Coordination

* Design and lead flagship convenings, including an annual research symposium that brings together leading researchers, clinicians, practitioners, and funders.
* Facilitate alignment and collaboration across academic institutions that are currently operating in parallel.
* Create structured forums for debate, synthesis, and agenda validation.
* Position the Foundation as a coordinator and catalyst—not a competitor to academic institutions.


3\. Research Governance, Rigor \& Independence

* Establish and oversee research governance structures, including Research Advisory Committees and peer review standards.
* Ensure funded, endorsed, or elevated research meets high standards of scientific rigor and ethical integrity.
* Protect scientific independence while maintaining relevance to elite sport environments.
* Define clear criteria for when and how research may involve NWSL athletes.


4\. Actionability \& Translation

* Ensure research questions and outputs are designed to be usable in practice, not solely academic.
* Partner with High Performance and Medical leadership to pressure\-test relevance and applicability.
* Support responsible translation of validated research into guidance, frameworks, or insights—without compromising independence or competitive integrity.


5\. Athlete\-Involved Research Oversight

* Establish disciplined protocols for research involving NWSL players, prioritizing player welfare, consent, and trust.
* Evaluate when athlete participation meaningfully advances the research agenda.
* Coordinate closely with League leadership, clubs, and the Players Association as appropriate.


6\. Fundraising \& External Partnerships

* Lead fundraising to sustain and scale the Foundation’s agenda\-setting work, including major gifts, aligned corporate partnerships, and research\-restricted funding.
* Inspire donors around impact, credibility, and long\-term field leadership—not transactional grantmaking.
* Develop integrated league moments (e.g., marquee convenings, designated matchweeks) that support fundraising without diluting mission.
* Represent the Foundation to philanthropic, academic, and institutional partners.

Duties Description Kirby Forensic Psychiatric Center (KFPC), an Office of Mental Health (OMH) forensic facility is recruiting a Deputy Director, Psychiatric Center 2 – Operations (DDPC 2 – Ops) to serve as the Director of Inpatient Services.
  

  

Duties
  

The Director of Inpatient Services serves as an essential member of KFPC’s Executive Leadership Team. Under the general direction of the Executive Director, the Director of Inpatient Services is responsible for the non\-medical clinical management of KFPC’s inpatient forensic hospital. The Director of Inpatient Services will design, develop, evaluate, and ensure the effective operations of all KFPC’s adult treatment programs including:
  

  

* Establishing and maintaining safe environments for patient care with a focus on evidence\-based programs, cultural competence, and community care.
* Participating in the development of KFPC’s short and long term goals.
* Establishing policies and procedures to ensure efficient and effective service delivery.
* Monitoring and overseeing staffing, assignments, and work schedules to ensure quality patient care.
* Ensuring service delivery complies with OMH guidelines, values, and regulatory agency standards.
* Maintaining working relationships with external organizations to maximize resources and implement program goals.
* Supervising and coordinating activities of subordinate managers.

  

  

  

  

Minimum Qualifications Education
  

Master's degree in a mental hygiene discipline (including physician assistant, occupational therapy, physical therapy, social work, speech pathology and audiology, communication disorders, psychology, recreation therapy, rehabilitation counseling, education, nursing), hospital administration, community mental health, business or public administration or other administrative area specifically related to health care, behavioral or social science or a valid license to practice medicine in New York State or Canada.
  

  

AND
  

  

Experience
  

Seven (7\) years of administrative, consultative, or supervisory experience in a mental health program, three (3\) years of which must have been managerial experience, including one or more of the following:
  

  

1\. One (1\) year of experience in a position comparable to Clinical Chief of Service or Director of Mental Health Rehabilitation;
  

  

OR
  

  

2\. Two (2\) years of experience in a position as administrative head of a multidisciplinary treatment team;
  

  

OR
  

  

3\. Two (2\) years of professional, supervisory, or administrative experience in the development, operation, and/or implementation of the mental health service delivery system for State facilities, counties, or local/private agencies in three (3\) or more of the following areas: program development, management procedures, community organization, resource planning, funding, program proposals, advisory boards, consumer and community advocacy and intergovernmental relations.
  

  

Additionally, all candidates must be eligible to participate in Federal health care programs (e.g., Medicaid). Individuals excluded from participation in these programs will not be considered.  

  



Additional Comments About KFPC
  

KFPC, located on Ward’s Island in New York City, provides inpatient treatment and rehabilitation to pretrial defendants who were deemed unfit to stand trial and were court ordered for restoration of fitness to stand trial and individuals who have been found not guilty by reason of insanity. KFPC is committed to supporting underserved individuals and delivering treatment with respect for each individual's privacy and rights along with activities and initiatives to reduce disparities in access, quality, and treatment for underserved populations.
  

  

About OMH
  

OMH operates the largest state mental health system in the country, with 23 hospitals, 90 clinics, two world\-class research institutes, a secure residential center, and a network of community services. OMH hospitals are all Joint Commission\-accredited and recognized as among the best mental health hospital systems in the United States. OMH believes everyone should have an equal opportunity to achieve mental wellness. This means implementing services and policies to reduce disparities in access, quality, and treatment outcomes for historically marginalized, underserved, and unserved populations.
  

If you would like to join KFPC and contribute to a workforce dedicated to public service, we offer:
  

* Generous paid time off, including thirteen (13\) vacation days, eight (8\) sick days, and five (5\) personal days accrued during the first year of employment; thirteen (13\) paid holidays each year.
* Option to choose a NYS health insurance plan that meets your needs.
* Dental and vision coverage.
* Enrollment in the New York State and Local Retirement System (NYSLRS) or a voluntary defined contribution plan.

  

Notes:
  

Plus $4,150 Location Pay.

Resolve cross\-department issues; assign work; monitor completion; and maintain continuity when staffing is limited. Recommend organizational improvements and sustainable service standards.

2\. Board and corporate governance. Prepare agendas, management reports, budgets, proposed policies, and decision materials with the President and Secretary\-Treasurer. Present accurate operational, financial, compliance, personnel, and risk information without obscuring adverse developments. Support meeting notices, elections, membership records, minutes, corporate filings, and required member communications while preserving the Secretary\-Treasurer's accountability. Implement approved actions and maintain an action\-item record. Obtain counsel's advice on governing documents, records requests, open\-government applicability, major transactions, and disputed authority. Maintain a current governing\-document and amendment register, distinguish charter requirements from ordinary bylaw quorum rules, and obtain legal review of election terms and adoption thresholds. Maintain complete approval records for each election, amendment, and corporate action.

3\. Financial stewardship. Develop annual operating and capital budgets and multiyear financial and asset\-replacement plans. Monitor revenue, cash flow, costs, reserves, debt service, covenant compliance, and budget variances. Coordinate bookkeeping, payroll, tax filings, financial statements, and the independent annual audit with qualified staff and advisers. Recommend rates, fees, deposits, and financial policies to the Board with supporting cost and affordability information; implement only lawfully adopted changes. Ensure invoices and payroll are accurate and timely, and maintain independent approval and reconciliation controls even when personally covering financial tasks.

4\. Funding, grants, and lender relations. Identify suitable financing, grants, technical assistance, and reimbursement opportunities. Coordinate applications, feasibility information, matching resources, environmental and procurement conditions, reporting, draw requests, and closeout. Track restricted funds and avoid commitments before required approval. Maintain productive relationships with lenders, grant administrators, and financial advisers. Do not promise funding or eligibility before verification or incur debt outside Board authority.

5\. Drinking\-water and environmental compliance. Maintain a complete register of the utility's facilities, permits, operating conditions, sampling and reporting duties, inspection findings, and renewal dates. Ensure adequate licensed treatment and distribution staffing and backup coverage appropriate to each system classification. Coordinate compliance with the Safe Drinking Water Act, applicable Florida DEP and other public\-health requirements, Northwest Florida Water Management District requirements, and other applicable authorities. Require qualified review of sampling, operational logs, consumer confidence reports, public notices, water\-use reports, cross\-connection control, and corrective actions. Track applicable lead and copper, PFAS, and other rule changes with qualified advisers, identifying each adopted requirement and its effective date. Oversee continuing service\-line inventory verification, updates, customer notices, replacement planning, and related funding documentation. Maintain current compliance and funding records.

6\. Operations and infrastructure. Oversee source\-water availability, treatment, storage, distribution pressure, water quality, metering, asset condition, preventive maintenance, inventory, fleet readiness, and water\-loss control through qualified staff. Review work orders, outages, repairs, inspections, alarm response, and maintenance backlogs. Plan timely replacement or expansion of wells, tanks, mains, pumps, controls, and other assets. Ensure current maps and asset records, physical security, appropriate easements and access, and reliable supply and repair arrangements. Do not promise fire\-flow capacity, system extensions, or new connections without technical and legal verification. Require field verification of mains recorded as inactive or abandoned, reconcile system maps and material inventories, and maintain valve, hydrant, backup\-power, and surge\-protect

new_jobs.title: Senior Director of Advancement Services
new_jobs.description:
**West Chester University Foundation**  

**Senior Director of Advancement Services**


*The West Chester University Foundation engages donors and other partners to drive student success. We secure funding that helps West Chester University students achieve more. More about the WCU Foundation can be found at* *https://www.wcufoundation.org/**.*




The West Chester University Foundation is currently looking for a **Senior Director of Advancement Services** to join its dedicated, dynamic and collaborative team! The Senior Director of Advancement Services provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for advancement systems, data, reporting, and gift administration functions in support of the West Chester University Foundation’s fundraising and engagement goals. This role is responsible for setting the long\-range vision and short\-term operational strategy for the Advancement Services department to strengthen alumni engagement and increase philanthropic support of the West Chester University Foundation.
Serving as a key member of the leadership team, the Senior Director partners closely with the senior Foundation and advancement leadership, Finance, campus partners, and external vendors to ensure that systems, data, and processes effectively support fundraising priorities and organizational growth.
As the Foundation prepares to support **West Chester University’s largest comprehensive fundraising campaign in history**, the Senior Director will play a critical role in ensuring that advancement systems, data, reporting, gift administration, and operational processes are scalable, accurate, and aligned to support the increased activity and complexity associated with a transformational campaign.


**Essential Job Functions:*** **Leadership and Strategic Oversight**
	+ Lead and guide the Advancement Services department, setting strategic priorities and fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
	+ Develop and execute long\-range plans for systems, processes, reporting, and analytics that support organizational fundraising goals.
	+ Partner with senior leadership to assess operational needs, align resources, and ensure data and systems strategy supports institutional priorities.
	+ Evaluate existing systems and emerging technologies to enhance data quality, accessibility, integration, reporting, and overall operational effectiveness.
* **Advancement Services \& Data Management**
	+ Provide strategic oversight for the administration, optimization, and governance of the Foundation’s advancement systems.
	+ Define and enforce policies, standards, and workflows to ensure data integrity, system effectiveness, and compliance with industry and institutional standards.
	+ Drive initiatives that enhance operational efficiency, reporting, and analytics capabilities.
	+ Collaborate with Finance, Development, and other stakeholders to ensure accurate gift processing and reporting.
	+ Partner with Donor Relations to ensure accurate data and reporting that support stewardship communications and donor recognition.
	+ Oversee the development and maintenance of documentation, reporting frameworks, and system protocols to support staff performance and organizational growth.
* **Prospect Strategy \& Data Support**
	+ Lead the prospect management function through strategic oversight of data, reporting, and system support.
	+ Collaborate with Development leadership to align prospect\-related workflows and reporting tools with fundraising priorities.

new_jobs.title: Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
**Executive Director Opportunity**

**Kokomo Rescue Mission \| Kokomo, Indiana**

Lead a trusted organization. Transform lives. Shape the future.

The Kokomo Rescue Mission is seeking an experienced and passionate Executive Director to lead a well established, Christ\-centered nonprofit into its next season of growth and impact.

Located in Kokomo, Indiana, a growing industrial city and farming community in north central Indiana, the Mission is approximately one hour north of Indianapolis.

Founded in 1953, the Kokomo Rescue Mission has more than 70 years of history serving individuals and families that are homeless and hurting. Today, the organization operates with an annual budget exceeding $3\.5 million, with approximately $1\.8 million coming through direct community donations. This is a testament to the strong relationships and confidence the Mission has built throughout the community.

The Mission operates three homeless shelters, serving men, women, and women with children. In 2025, the Mission provided an average of 326 meals each day and served an average of 122 overnight guests each night.

The organization is also entering an exciting new chapter of community engagement. Its new Engagement Center expands the Mission’s reach beyond traditional shelter services by providing practical assistance, connecting individuals with community partners and resources, and offering showers and laundry facilities to the broader community.

The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to lead a respected organization with a strong foundation, committed staff, generous community support, and significant potential for continued growth.

This leader will help shape the Mission’s future while strengthening its ministry, expanding community partnerships, stewarding its resources, developing its team, and ensuring that the organization remains focused on its calling to serve the homeless and hurting.

For the right leader, this is more than an executive position. It is an opportunity to step into a 70\+ year legacy, lead a growing nonprofit, build upon strong community relationships, and help shape the future of social services in Kokomo and beyond.

If you are a strategic, relational, mission\-driven leader who is ready to make a lasting difference, we invite you to consider joining the Kokomo Rescue Mission by submitting your resume to ksalsbery@rescuekokomo.org or visit our website at https://kokomorescuemission.org/

**Position Summary:**

The Executive Director of the Kokomo Rescue Mission provides strategic leadership, ensuring the organization's vision, programs, and financial sustainability align with its mission. He or She oversees staff, fundraising efforts, and community relations while advocating for the Mission’s work and securing resources. Additionally, the Executive Director ensures compliance with regulations, manages crisis situations, and leads long\-term strategic planning for the organization's growth and impact.

**Core Competencies:**

* Teamwork
* Operations Management
* Personnel Management
* Spiritual Leadership
* Financial Management
* Development
* Administrative Oversight

**Primary Duties and Responsibilities (includes but not limited to):**

**Administrative Duties:**

* Responsible for the spiritual environment and growth of all Mission programs by approving the development of new programs as necessary to meet the needs of the community.
* Evaluate current programs to see if they still are reaching the needs of the community.
* Prepare for and attend Board of Director's meetings and executive committee meetings.
* Carry out Mission policy; create the same in emergency situations where needed.
* Recommend to the Board new or significant changes to ministries.
* Attend skill and spiritual enrichment conferences and seminars that will benefit the Mission.

**Operational Management:**

* Have a comprehensive knowledge of the principles and practices of program, personnel, and budget administration necessary to the efficient operation of the entire organization.
* Hire and terminate employees. Responsible for hiring the right people into leadership.
* Responsible for the operation of administrative and departmental functions according to the Organizational Chart.
* Meet with the Lead Team on a regular basis to maintain effective communication within the ministry.
* Maintain continuous interface with leadership to insure proper and effective staffing in order to carry out the Mission’s purposes.
* Administer evaluations for the staff that directly report to the Executive Director and maintain a salary review program.
* Assess need and implement necessary staff education.
* Preside over weekly staff meetings.

**Public Relations Duties:**

* Represent KRM through speaking engagements, conferences, church groups, service clubs, other community organizations, television, radio, and newspaper interviews.
* Network with community leaders, businessmen, industrial executives, etc.
* Cooperate with governmental and other private help organizations in assisting those in need.

**Financial Duties:**

* Be ultimately responsible for Mission finances.
* Oversee the fundraising initiatives and campaigns of the organization.
* Direct preparation of Annual Budget for Board approval.
* Work with Staff in preparing the final operating budgets for approval by the Board of Directors and regularly monitor financial reports to see that the departments stay within the budget parameters.
* Review monthly financial reports and be prepared to answer any questions that arise at Board meetings.
* See that the Mission acknowledges all donations to the ministry with a receipt and thank you.

**Education or Skill Set:**

* Bachelor’s degree preferred in nonprofit management, business administration, public administration, organizational leadership, social work, human services, ministry/theology, or a related field and/or minimum of 5 years of executive leadership experience in a related field.

new_jobs.title: Administrator/Executive Director - West Branch
new_jobs.description:
Baruch Senior Ministries is seeking a dynamic and compassionate Administrator to lead our Horizon Senior Living of West Branch facility in West Branch, MI \- a compassionate, resident\-centered community dedicated to providing high\-quality care and services to older adults. The Administrator will be responsible for overseeing all aspects of the facility’s operations, including strategic planning, staff management, budgeting, compliance, and most importantly, creating an environment where residents feel valued, comfortable, and at home.
The ideal candidate will have a passion for senior care, possess strong leadership abilities, and demonstrate a commitment to ensuring the highest standards of care and service for our residents.
**Key Responsibilities:**
* **Leadership \& Management:**


Lead, motivate, and manage a team of staff including caregivers, food service, and support staff. Foster a culture of collaboration, respect, and teamwork within the facility. Ensure that all team members are properly trained and have the resources they need to succeed.
* **Operational Oversight:**


Oversee the day\-to\-day operations of the facility, ensuring that the facility meets all regulatory requirements, safety standards, and quality of care expectations. Implement and evaluate policies and procedures for resident care, daily operations, and staff performance.
* **Resident Care \& Satisfaction:**


Ensure that residents receive personalized care that respects their dignity, preferences, and needs. Monitor resident satisfaction and make improvements as necessary. Address resident and family concerns in a timely and empathetic manner.
* **Financial Management:**


Develop and manage the facility's budget, monitor financial performance, and ensure that operations remain financially viable. Implement strategies to optimize revenue while controlling costs. Assist in fundraising and securing resources to support the facility’s mission.
* **Community Relations:**


Represent the facility in the local community, including participating in outreach programs, building relationships with local healthcare providers, and promoting the facility’s services.
**Qualifications:**
* A passion for caring for our residents as they age.
* Bachelor’s degree required \- Master's degree preferred.
* A minimum of 5 years of experience in senior living or healthcare management, with at least 3 years in a leadership role.
* Strong knowledge of local, state, and federal regulations related to assisted living and long\-term care.
* Proven experience in budgeting, financial management, and strategic planning.
* Excellent interpersonal, communication, and leadership skills.


**About Baruch Senior Ministries:**
Baruch Senior Ministries is a faith\-based, nonprofit organization dedicated to honoring God by serving people as they age. We have 28 assisted living facilities across the state of Michigan that seek to care for the elderly and uphold Biblical principles. We understand that the value and quality of our care heavily relies upon the ability and passion of our employees. Every person has unique, valuable gifts that can be used to effectively provide our residents with the best care. We are an equal opportunity employer that does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. If you share our commitment to honoring God through our work and delivering quality care to all our residents, then we invite you to join our team.

new_jobs.description:

The Executive Director leads Big Brothers Big Sisters of Fond du Lac County to ensure the agency's mission, strategy, values, and goals are achieved — and that our mentoring programs serve the youth of Fond du Lac County effectively and sustainably. * Entrepreneurial approach to limited resources

You'll lead an organization with a proven, measurable impact on kids in our community — with the support of an engaged Board and a passionate staff team behind you.

* Bachelor's (Required)

Experience:

* Nonprofit sector: 7 years (Required)

Work Location: In person

new_jobs.description:
Innovative Human Rights NGO Seeks Global Executive Director

About Asylum Access

We are human rights advocates who support forcibly displaced individuals and communities as they reclaim their rights, agency and power.

Our unique combination of legal empowerment, policy advocacy and global systems change creates conditions in which refugees can live safely, move freely, work on fair terms and go to school in supportive environments.

Our work transforms the traditional approach of endless humanitarian handouts to a sustainable solution that honors refugees’ freedom, dignity and autonomy, and empowers them to make choices about their own lives.

Asylum Access’ global team and family of local civil society organizations advocate to make human rights a reality for refugees around the world. Our national organizations are led and staffed primarily by community members in those countries, and there is strong mutual trust and respect between us and our clients. On the international stage, we work with established institutions to shift the global system to better uphold and promote refugees’ human rights. We can help catalyze and lead systemic transformation because, uniquely among NGOs in the refugee response sector, we focus exclusively on rights and governance.

Position Description

The global Executive Director is responsible for ensuring the Asylum Access family of organizations fulfills and advances Asylum Access’ mission around the world. This includes leading the organization’s global systems change portfolio; positioning the global organization to support strategic and effective national\-level legal empowerment and policy advocacy by Asylum Access national organizations; and guiding the organization in creating and pursuing a bold, cohesive vision toward a world where all displaced people enjoy all of their human rights.

Asylum Access values a collaborative approach to leadership. The global Executive Director is expected to work in close partnership with the national Executive Directors, who lead strategy and implementation of the mission at Asylum Access national organizations, to shape global organizational strategy, priorities, and performance. All four Executive Directors are responsible for stewarding Asylum Access’ vision and role within the global refugee response ecosystem; setting and executing organizational strategy within their particular remits and collaboratively across the global family of organizations; overseeing budgets and resource allocation; and ensuring strong programs, operations, and teams.

The successful candidate for global Executive Director will be visionary in outlook, with a broad understanding of displacement dynamics and political trends around the world – particularly in and affecting Africa, Asia and Latin America, where most refugees remain. They will be deeply collaborative in approach. They understand the importance of shared enthusiasm as a driving force, and the necessity of a cohesive leadership team to achieve meaningful impact in challenging circumstances. They are committed to understanding and supporting the contexts in which Asylum Access organizations currently work, and to identifying and advancing efforts in other contexts if/as this has the potential to magnify Asylum Access’ impact in creating the world we envision.

The global Executive Director is hired by, reports to, and serves at the pleasure of the Board of Directors, in accordance with the organization’s bylaws, and may serve as a nonvoting, *ex officio* member of the Board.

Essential Job Responsibilities

Key components of the global Executive Director role include, without limitation:

*Strategic Visioning and Leadership*

* With a consistent eye on the future, continually gather information and assess trends relevant to Asylum Access’ mission, and guide the organization to adapt accordingly – bearing in mind Asylum Access’ historic role at the forefront of paradigm shifts and operational innovations that support displaced people to reclaim their rights, agency and power.
* Together with staff and board leadership, and in consultation as appropriate with other stakeholders inside and outside the organization, craft and carry out a strategic vision in line with Asylum Access’ mission and values. This includes the development of theories of change and the development and implementation of multi\-year strategic, operational, and annual plans.
* Ensure the entire family of Asylum Access organizations maintains coherence and consistency with the organization’s mission, vision, values, and brand.
* Envision and develop governance structures that align with Asylum Access’ deep commitment to shifting power dynamics in service of a shared leadership model. This includes building consensus among the Executive Director team for decisions with organization\-wide impact.
* Inspire, motivate, and catalyze the development of staff at all levels of the organization.

*Global Oversight*

* Steward the cohesion of the global leadership team and the culture of collaborative leadership across the organization.
* Provide support and administrative supervision to National Executive Directors, and manage the hiring, onboarding, and termination of these positions in accordance with Asylum Access’ human resources protocols.
* Together with the National Executive Directors, lead oversight of Asylum Access’ impact to ensure all programs and advocacy are aligned with human rights principles and designed to effectively achieve Asylum Access’ mission, vision, and goals.

*Reputation and Influence*

* Steward and advance Asylum Access’ global reputation as a well\-known refugee human rights organization and as an important and effective actor in displacement response, human rights, and migration fields. In particular, give voice to on\-the\-ground impact within national organizations – and partner organizations where requested and appropriate – in international dialogue.

new_jobs.title: Director of Communications & Brand
new_jobs.description:
**Job Summary:**

The Director of Communications \& Brand is responsible for the strategic leadership of GEDP's communications, brand, and content function, shaping the organization's narrative, stewarding its visual and editorial identity, and ensuring that GEDP's work and impact are clearly and compellingly communicated to every audience it serves. The Director is the senior editorial, creative, and communications voice of the organization.

The Director leads a team of two manager\-level individual contributors — a Lead Designer and a Content \& Social Media Manager — and provides active creative direction, editorial oversight, and day\-to\-day management to both. The Director is not a production role; it is a leadership role that sets the creative and strategic direction the team executes against. This includes direct art direction of the Lead Designer's work, editorial direction of all content across GEDP's channels, and strategic oversight of GEDP's full digital and communications presence. GEDP anticipates adding a Content \& Social Media Coordinator as the function grows.

The Director of Communications \& Brand will lead GEDP through a significant period of organizational growth and public visibility, including an organizational rebrand, a capital campaign, and a destination marketing effort in partnership with the City of Easton. The Director serves as GEDP's primary liaison to outside communications, marketing, brand, and creative agency relationships.

**Job Duties \& Responsibilities:**

**Brand Strategy \& Organizational Narrative**

* Leads GEDP through an organizational rebrand in collaboration with the Executive Director, board, and outside creative partners; ensures the new identity reflects the organization's mission, voice, and strategic ambitions across all programs, events, and sub\-brands
* Serves as primary staff liaison to the destination marketing firm engaged by GEDP and the City of Easton, providing institutional knowledge, content, and quality oversight
* Develops and stewards GEDP's brand standards, tone of voice, and messaging architecture across all channels, programs, and audiences — including GEDP\-wide communications, the Easton Public Market, the Easton Farmers' Market, and other program\-specific presences
* Champions GEDP's commitment to design that is intentional, human, and rooted — actively resisting generic, corporate, or AI\-inflated visual and written output across all organizational materials
* Articulates GEDP's and Easton's identity — as a destination, a community, and a civic model — in language and images that resonate with residents, visitors, investors, and funders

**Creative Direction \& Team Leadership**

* Provides active, hands\-on art direction to the Lead Designer — not approval of finished work, but engagement in the creative process: reviewing concepts, pushing quality, ensuring visual output reflects GEDP's brand sensibility and the handmade, craft\-influenced aesthetic the organization values
* Provides editorial direction to the Content \& Social Media Manager across all content channels — setting voice, approving strategy, reviewing key content, and ensuring the work reflects organizational priorities and brand standards

For more than 170 years, Elwyn has been leading the way in supporting children, teens, and adults with autism, intellectual and developmental disabilities, and behavioral health challenges. Now, we’re looking for passionate team members to join us. Here, your work will change lives – including your own. You’ll make an impact every day, find purpose in what you do, and grow in a career that truly matters.  

At Elwyn, we take care of you while you care for others. We offer:* Generous Paid Time Off

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world\-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.

Harvard Medical School's mission is to nurture a diverse, inclusive community dedicated to alleviating suffering and improving health and well\-being for all through excellence in teaching and learning, discovery and scholarship, and service and leadership.


You’ll be at the heart of biomedical discovery, education, and innovation, working alongside world\-renowned faculty and a community dedicated to improving human health. This is more than a job \- it’s an opportunity to shape the future of medicine.

The Executive Director will serve as the primary visionary, ensuring that every camper and staff member experiences a transformative and joyful environment aligned with our mission. The ideal candidate will bring energetic leadership, excellent organizational skills, and a deep commitment to youth development and Christian values.

EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR: CAMPING AND RETREAT MINISTRIES

The New York Annual Conference of the United Methodist Church is seeking a full\-time Executive Director of our Camping and Retreat Ministries.

The Executive Director of Camping and Retreat Ministries (“CRM”) is the on\-site Director of Quinipet Camp and Retreat Center, a year\-round facility on Shelter Island, NY with oversight and support for Kingswood Campsite, a seasonal campsite in Hancock, NY. The CRM provides a sacred space apart from the everyday world where all are welcomed to experience God’s creation. CRM encourages Christian community and spiritual growth through overnight summer camp and year round retreats, and works to develop and nurture the leaders of tomorrow. The Executive Director guides staff and volunteers in partnership with the Camps Governing Board to accomplish overall goals.

Principal Duties and Tasks include: Oversight of two locations in New York state; administration and management of regular and seasonal staff, and budgets and financial records; maintenance and management of properties and facilities; marketing to and recruitment of clientele and staff; development of long term goals for expansion of all programs; maintain risk and regulatory government and UMC standards; attendance and participation in monthly Governing Board and Task Force meetings, and New York Annual Conference meeting in June.

Applicants must possess a Bachelor’s Degree (Master’s degree preferred) and have at least 5\-10 years of experience in managing a Christian camping environment or related experience. Member of a United Methodist Church (preferred) or possess significant understanding of UM doctrine and polity. Commitment to working in a Christian environment. Acceptance of and ability to communicate with people of various religious affiliations, ethnicities, genders, ages, and differing abilities is vitally important. Excellent computer skills, including working knowledge of QuickBooks. Experience with CampMinder and Gazebo registration systems is a plus. Must agree to live on\-site, year\-round at Camp Quinipet, on Shelter Island, NY. Some travel within New York Annual Conference area is expected.

A three bedroom, two bath, 1400 sq. ft. house and basic utilities are included in the compensation package, which also includes health insurance, pension, and other employee benefits.

To learn more about the New York Annual Conference please visit us at: www.nyac.com

To apply, please send a cover letter, resume

**Duties**

* Provide strategic direction for all camp ministries, ensuring alignment with organizational mission and values.
* Lead recruitment, training, supervision, and evaluation of camp staff and volunteers, fostering a team\-oriented culture focused on safety, engagement, and spiritual growth.
* Oversee the planning and execution of diverse youth programs including outdoor activities, arts, theater experiences, tutoring sessions, and youth group activities.
* Ensure compliance with all safety protocols including first aid procedures, CPR/AED operation, behavior management policies, and child supervision standards.

**Experience**

* Proven experience working with children in educational or recreational settings; prior camp experience is highly preferred.
